tickets.background:
Phase P0 establishes the foundational specification for the siprs crate: M20 priority map (N0002), non-goals and Tauri boundary (N0003), terminology (N0004), compliance requirements (N0005), versioning policy (N0006), 15 functional requirements (N0007), and module structure (N0008). These 7 specification nodes constrain all subsequent implementation.

### Goal
Produce a complete, self-contained specification document (`specs/P0-1.md`) that fully documents all 7 RFC foundation nodes (N0002-N0008) with Goal/Purpose/Motivation/Constraints per node, cross-reference consistency, and contract testability. The spec serves as the single source of truth for all downstream P0 and PX implementation tickets.

### Purpose
Establish the normative foundation that constrains every subsequent implementation decision in the siprs crate. Without this foundation, 8 downstream tickets (P0-2 through P0-8) would operate without a shared understanding of priorities (N0002), boundaries (N0003), terminology (N0004), compliance constraints (N0005/N0006), requirements scope (N0007), and architecture (N0008). The spec ensures all implementers share the same design context.

### Motivation
The siprs crate has 8 P0 tickets and 60+ architecture/spec files already created (under src/api/, src/config/, src/model/, src/state/, etc.), but no unified specification document that ties these fragments together and validates completeness. Without P0-1, downstream work risks inconsistencies (e.g., a module implementing a feature that N0003 excludes as a non-goal, or a codec not listed in N0007's 15 FRs). This ticket prevents that drift by committing the foundation to a reviewable, version-controlled spec.

### Constraints
- Time: P0-1 must be completed before P0-2 through P0-8 can begin implementation (dependency chain).
- Scope: Must cover exactly N0002-N0008. N0001 (§1 Purpose) and N0009 (§7 Concurrency) are scoped to P0-3 and P0-2 respectively — P0-1 only references them as graph edges.
- Format: Spec output is Markdown (`specs/P0-1.md`). No executable code is produced by this ticket (except the stub at `src/config/versioning_policy.rs` which is intentionally placeholder).
- Validation: All 15 contracts must pass Gate M verification. No contract may have an untestable Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant triple.

  - [Action: add/modify/remove/rename/refactor] **add** — create new specification file
  - [What specifically changes] A standalone spec document is created from Tickets.json fields, RFC graph data, and node context. No existing source code is modified (the only code file, `src/config/versioning_policy.rs`, remains as a stub — its expansion is a downstream implementation ticket)
  - [Before → After (behavior/signature)] Before: no unified spec exists. After: `specs/P0-1.md` contains complete documentation of N0002-N0008.
  - [API contract change (if any)] None — this ticket produces no Rust API changes.
  - [Data schema change (if any)] None — only the Tickets.json P0-1 entry is populated with spec fields.
  - [Config/env change (if any)] None — no Cargo.toml, env vars, or build config changes.
  - [Dependency added/removed (if any)] None — no crate dependencies added.

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - [Excluded item] N0001 (§1 Purpose — Responsibilities of this crate) full specification
  - [Why excluded — separate ticket / future phase / not applicable] Scoped to P0-3 (Crate Purpose & Scope Definition). P0-1 only references N0001 as the target of graph edges from N0002-N0008.
  - [Excluded item] N0009 (§7 Concurrency Model & Execution Contexts) detail
  - [Why excluded — separate ticket / future phase / not applicable] Scoped to P0-2 (Concurrency Model & Execution Contexts Specification). P0-1 only documents the N0008→N0009 (depends_on) edge.
  - [Excluded item] Code generation, build.rs changes, or runtime behavior
  - [Why excluded — separate ticket / future phase / not applicable] This is a pure specification ticket. N0006 code stub expansion is deferred to the implementation ticket that resolves the `[::STUB::]` marker.
  - [Excluded item] CI/CD pipeline, Docker images, or prebuilt infrastructure
  - [Why excluded — separate ticket / future phase / not applicable] Scoped to P2/P3-phase tickets (referenced by N0039→N0005 inbound edge C040).

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - [Affected component] Downstream P0 tickets (P0-2 through P0-8)
  - [Nature of impact: performance / security / API surface / data format / …] **Data format** — all downstream tickets must reference this spec as their normative foundation. The module structure (N0008) defines file paths that P0-4 through P0-8 will implement.
  - [Corresponding change needed Y/N + details] **No code change needed** in downstream tickets at this point. However, each downstream ticket's `referenceSection` and `relatedTicketIds` must be updated during their own make phase to reference P0-1.
  - [Affected component] `RFC-ROOT-GRAPH.json` edge relationships
  - [Nature of impact: performance / security / API surface / data format / …] **Validation** — the spec existence validates that the edges from N0002-N0008 to N0001 are correctly documented.
  - [Corresponding change needed Y/N + details] No — the graph is already complete for these nodes.
  - [Affected component] Cargo.toml (`rust-version = "1.95"`)
  - [Nature of impact: performance / security / API surface / data format / …] **Compliance** — MSRV 1.95 is documented as a compliance requirement (N0005).
  - [Corresponding change needed Y/N + details] Already satisfied. No change needed.

testExceptions:
- [Item] Automated Rust unit tests for N0006 src/config/versioning_policy.rs
  - [Reason] The file is currently a stub (pub struct Config {} with STUB marker) and is not testable as automated Rust unit tests — it has no behavior to test until implemented with actual version-policy enforcement logic. Unit tests will be added in the implementation ticket that resolves this stub.
  - [Why this is NOT a design defect] The stub is an intentional placeholder — this is not a design defect. The Config struct will gain behavior when the versioning policy rules are implemented in a downstream ticket. The current empty struct is a valid Rust pattern for gradual implementation. The spec (P0-1) documents the design; it does not implement runtime code.
  - [Alternative verification] Spec presence verified by test -f src/config/versioning_policy.rs. Stub marker verified by grep STUB src/config/versioning_policy.rs. Cross-reference to N0006 verified by checking the Initial Design Artifact header contains NODE-ID N0006.

- [Item] Automated validation of spec cross-references across all 7 nodes
  - [Reason] No validation harness exists in P0 phase, making automated cross-reference validation impossible to test via CI. Building an automated cross-reference auditor is a separate investment (P3 or later infrastructure ticket). In P0, cross-reference consistency is verified via manual review.
  - [Why this is NOT a design defect] Absence of an automated validation tool is an infrastructure gap, not a design defect. The spec document is still testable through manual review — a proven method for specification verification. The project's RFC graph structure provides machine-readable edges that could be leveraged by a future tool.
  - [Alternative verification] Manual review checklist: (1) each node section header matches RFC-ROOT.md anchor, (2) each graph edge documented in spec has a visible cross-reference link, (3) no orphan section references.

- [Item] End-to-end verification that all 15 functional requirements (N0007) are implementable
  - [Reason] Implementability verification is not testable until all 8 downstream tickets (P0-2 through P0-8, PX tickets) are completed. A requirement can only be confirmed as implementable once its concrete code mapping exists.
  - [Why this is NOT a design defect] This is a sequential dependency, not a design defect. N0007 functional requirements are intentionally documented at the specification level — their implementability is verified incrementally as each downstream ticket delivers code.
  - [Alternative verification] Each functional requirement includes: (a) unique identifier (FR-01 through FR-15), (b) reference to implementing module path, (c) mapping to downstream ticket(s). Completeness verified by acceptance criteria checklist.

**[Happy path] The spec file `specs/P0-1.md` is generated with complete content for all 7 nodes (N0002-N0008). Each node section includes: RFC source reference, purpose statement, key data (tables/lists), cross-reference links, and contractual mappings. All 15 contracts pass Gate M. The spec is internally consistent (no contradictory statements across nodes).**
  - All 11 Tickets.json spec fields are populated (no template stubs remain)
  - `specs/P0-1.md` exists and is >500 lines
  - `verify-make-contracts.js --ticket-key=P0-1` exits 0
  - Cross-references between N0002-N0008 match RFC-ROOT-GRAPH.json edges

**[Error case] Spec generation detects incomplete or inconsistent data. For example: a contract's Invariant references a type that doesn't exist in any N0002-N0008 node, or a scope item lists a path outside the allowed module tree.**
  - The spec generation process (`--for-spec`) handles missing data gracefully by reporting gaps
  - Contracts with unresolved inbound edges are flagged but not rejected (since their source tickets are future work)
  - Incomplete sections are documented as open items, not silently omitted

**[Edge case] Edge case: a spec node has no substantive content beyond its RFC reference (e.g., N0004 Terminology is a short glossary).**
  - Minimum content standard: each node must have at least 3 substantively different sections (definition, RFC reference, relationship description)
  - Short nodes are acceptable as long as they cover Goal/Purpose/Motivation minimally
  - The cross-reference edges between nodes provide the substantive content even for individually short nodes

tickets.investigation:
- Investigation findings for P0-1 (RFC Foundation & Crate Specification):

**Source code structure:** The siprs crate has no `lib.rs` or `client.rs` yet — all 40+ files under `src/` are architecture/specification documents organized by domain (api/, build/, concurrency_contexts/, config/, error/, model/, security/, state/, tests/). The only file with a direct N0006 code mapping is `src/config/versioning_policy.rs` which contains `pub struct Config {}` with a `[::STUB::]` marker.

**RFC graph completeness:** The 7 nodes N0002-N0008 are fully defined in `RFC-ROOT.md` (§§1a/2/3/4/4.1/5/6) and `RFC-ROOT-GRAPH.json`. All graph edges between these nodes and N0001 are documented. Inbound edges from downstream nodes (N0009→N0008, N0013→N0005, N0039→N0005, N0052→N0007, N0057→N0007, N0059→N0008, N0066→N0006) are present with correct source/target references.

**Key relationships discovered:**
- N0002 (M20 map) → refines N0001: The 15 implementation items and 14 design decisions are the most detailed content in this group.
- N0003 (Non-goals) → constrains N0001: 8 non-goals explicitly listed, plus 4+4 Tauri responsibility split.
- N0005 (Compliance) → constrains N0001: MSRV=1.95 already in Cargo.toml `rust-version`, PJSIP=2.17 documented but no `build.rs` yet, 3 OS targets specified.
- N0006 (Versioning) → part_of N0005: 0.x/1.0+ semver rules fully specified; `#[non_exhaustive]` is the key invariant mechanism.
- N0007 (15 FRs) → implements N0001: No FR-IDs assigned yet; FRs need unique identifiers for traceability.
- N0008 (Module structure) → part_of N0001: Complete file tree specified with 25+ files across 6 directories; single-crate rationale with 3 justifications.

**No existing stub violations found** in the files examined — the `[::STUB::]` marker in versioning_policy.rs is properly placed and documented.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Boy Scout Rule — Translatability improvements for P0-1:

**Code touched:** `src/config/versioning_policy.rs` (the only implementation file in scope)

**Current state:** The file contains `pub struct Config {}` with a `[::STUB::]` marker. It passes readability standards because its content is intentionally minimal — the struct name `Config` conveys "configuration placeholder" and the stub marker is properly documented.

**Planned improvements for when the stub is resolved (future ticket):**
1. Extract versioning phases into an enum: `pub enum VersioningPhase { PreRelease, Stable(Version), }` — makes versioning state machine explicit.
2. Name the version policy rules as named constants: `const ALLOW_BREAKING_IN_0_X: bool = true` instead of magic boolean literals.
3. Add `#[non_exhaustive]` to any enum that may gain variants in the future (aligned with N0006 invariant).

**No immediate refactoring needed:** The current code is 31 lines including comments and the Initial Design Artifact header. The `Config` struct is intentionally empty. Adding premature logic or structure here would violate YAGNI.

**Broader improvement (spec level):** The spec document generated by this ticket should use consistent section naming across all 7 nodes (each node section: ## Node Title → ### Purpose → ### Details → ### Cross-references → ### Contracts). This structural consistency is itself a translatability improvement — any reader can predict where to find information for any node.

tickets.background:
N0009 defines the four execution contexts (User async, Core reactor, PJSIP callbacks, Audio worker tasks), the core reactor thread model, and command serialization via unbounded MPSC. This is the threading foundation for the entire crate.

### Goal
Produce a complete specification document for siprs concurrency model, covering the four execution contexts, single-reactor threading architecture, RuntimeCommand serialization pattern, and the Send+Sync contract rationale.

### Purpose
The concurrency model is the architectural spine of the siprs crate. PJSUA (PJSIP) is a C library that spawns internal native threads and fires callbacks from them — the public Rust API must never execute directly on those callback threads. This spec defines the isolation boundaries and serialization strategy that make a safe async Rust wrapper possible.

### Motivation
The choice of execution context model, thread count, and command serialization determines every subsequent design decision (FFI wrappers, audio pipeline, state management). Without a precisely documented concurrency model, implementors have no basis for reasoning about thread safety, lock ordering, or the Send+Sync boundary. This specification must be written before any implementation code (P2).

### Constraints
- PJSUA thread safety: certain pjsua_* APIs must be called from the same thread; the spec must document how this is guaranteed via MPSC serialization.
- Single-reactor scalability ceiling: ~30 concurrent calls; the 100-accounts/300-calls threshold for partitioning is documented but not implemented.
- No unsafe code escapes ffi/ module (Rule C038).
- Audio RT callback prohibits blocking operations, allocations, or .await calls.
- The spec must be a standalone document — no external references that expire.
scope: Four execution contexts with their threading and async characteristics
Core reactor single-thread model with justification for ~30 concurrent call scalability
RuntimeCommand enum and unbounded MPSC serialization pattern

- [Path] src/concurrency_contexts/command_serialization.rs — Add the full RuntimeCommand enum definition with 10 variants, oneshot reply channels, and doc comments.
- [Action] Modify — Replace the stub `pub trait Service {}` with the actual RuntimeCommand enum and supporting type aliases (CommandSender, CommandReceiver).
- [Detail] Define `pub(crate) enum RuntimeCommand` with Initialize, AddAccount, RemoveAccount, SetRegistration, MakeCall, Hangup, Hold, Unhold, SendDtmf, Shutdown. Each variant carries a `reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<T, SipError>>`. Add `pub(crate) type CommandSender = tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<RuntimeCommand>` and `pub(crate) type CommandReceiver = tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<RuntimeCommand>`.
- [Before → After] `pub trait Service {}` (empty stub) → Complete RuntimeCommand enum with full doc comments explaining each variant, Send+Sync auto-derive, and module-level documentation of the four execution contexts.
- [API contract] No public API change — RuntimeCommand is `pub(crate)`. External consumers interact via the SipClient facade (P0-5). Adds implicit Send+Sync bound on all dependency types.
- [Schema] No data schema change. All command payload types (ClientConfig, AccountConfig, etc.) are defined in their respective P0-* tickets as stubs; the spec documents their required shape.
- [Config] No configuration change. The concurrency model (single reactor, unbounded MPSC) is hard-coded and not configurable.
- [Dep] No new dependencies. Uses tokio (mpsc, oneshot, sync) which is a crate-level dependency declared in P0-1.

- [Excluded item] Multi-reactor partitioning for >300 concurrent calls.
- [Why excluded] Explicitly out of scope per RFC §7.1a. The single-reactor model covers the target use case (Tauri desktop, AI phone agent, ~30 calls). Partitioning would require redesigning PJSUA thread safety assumptions and is deferred indefinitely.

- [Excluded item] Audio worker task implementation (AudioWorkerTask, AudioMixer).
- [Why excluded] The concurrency spec defines the RT boundary and lock-free queue contract (C034), but the audio worker implementation belongs to P0-8 (AudioMixer) and P2.

- [Affected component] runtime/ module — The reactor thread and command dispatch loop are implemented in runtime/. The spec defines the interface (RuntimeCommand, CommandSender) that runtime/ consumes.
- [Nature of impact] Architecture — The entire crate threading model is determined by this spec. All subsequent modules (ffi/, audio/) must conform to the execution context boundaries defined here.
- [Corresponding change needed] lib.rs: Add `pub mod concurrency_contexts;` declaration. Provide module-level doc re-exporting the execution context model. No further changes needed at this stage.
testUnit: UT: [Normal — Execution Contexts] Verify that the spec documents four distinct execution contexts — User async (tokio task), Core reactor (std::thread::JoinHandle), PJSIP native callbacks (C callback), and Audio worker tasks (tokio blocking pool or dedicated thread) — each with its threading model, responsibilities, and communication boundaries clearly defined.

UT: [Normal — RuntimeCommand Enum Definition] Verify that the spec defines RuntimeCommand with all 10 variants: Initialize(ClientConfig), AddAccount(AccountConfig), RemoveAccount(AccountId), SetRegistration(AccountId, bool), MakeCall(AccountId, OutgoingCallRequest), Hangup(CallId, HangupReason), Hold(CallId), Unhold(CallId), SendDtmf(CallId, String, DtmfMethod), Shutdown. Each variant must include a reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<T, SipError>> field.

UT: [Normal — MPSC Channel Type] Verify that the spec specifies tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<RuntimeCommand> for the command sender side and tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<RuntimeCommand> for the reactor receiver side, ensuring unbounded queue capacity for backpressure tolerance.
UT: [Normal — Send+Sync Guarantee] Verify that the spec documents how the MPSC serialization pattern provides Send+Sync on the public API without exposing PJSUA internal thread safety constraints.

UT: [Error — Invalid Command Rejection] Verify that the spec documents that a RuntimeCommand sent after Shutdown MUST be silently dropped or rejected with a dedicated SipErrorKind::RuntimeShutdown variant, preventing use-after-shutdown.

UT: [Boundary — Oneshot Exactly-Once Semantics] Verify that the spec documents that each oneshot::Sender MUST be consumed exactly once — sending via a consumed sender is a panic (documented as a programming error), and dropping a sender without sending causes the receiver to observe RecvError::Closed.

UT: [Boundary — Scalability Ceiling] Verify that the spec documents the ~30 simultaneous call scalability ceiling for the single-reactor thread model, including the reasoning (Tauri desktop / AI phone agent use case) and the conditions under which reactor partitioning would be considered (100+ accounts, 300+ concurrent calls).

UT: [Boundary — Audio Worker Lock-Free Boundary] Verify that the spec documents that Audio worker → PJSIP callback communication MUST use a lock-free queue (crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue) with no blocking operations permitted in the real-time callback path.

UT: [Contract C002 — Purpose via Async Model] Verify that the spec documents how the concurrency model enables the crate purpose (async-first SIP client) via: (a) User async context for public API consumers, (b) Core reactor for PJSUA control serialization, (c) Async interface for audio streaming. Invariant: reactor thread model is documented as single-threaded and immutable in the current major version.

UT: [Contract C010 — Module Boundary Fit] Verify that the spec documents how each execution context maps to the crate module structure: concurrency_contexts/ for model definition, runtime/ for reactor and command dispatch, audio/ for worker tasks. Invariant: reactor MUST be documented as single-threaded (std::thread::JoinHandle).

UT: [Contract C011 — RuntimeCommand Serialization] Verify that the spec documents the complete RuntimeCommand enum in concurrency_contexts::command_serialization, with each variant carrying a oneshot reply channel. Invariant: all operations that touch PJSUA state MUST be documented to go through the MPSC channel.

UT: [Contract C012 — Send+Sync Public API] Verify that the spec documents that the SipClient public API (SipClient struct in lib.rs) is Send + Sync. Invariant: the spec MUST NOT document any PJSUA thread safety details in the public API surface — those remain internal to ffi/.

UT: [Contract C034 — Audio Worker RT Boundary] Verify that the spec documents: (a) AudioWorkerTask per AudioMixer instance, (b) lock-free queue (crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue) for frame transfer, (c) no allocation/blocking in PJSIP RT callback. Invariant: lock-free queue is the only communication mechanism crossing the RT boundary.

UT: [Contract C038 — FFI Isolation] Verify that the spec documents that all unsafe PJSIP FFI bindings reside in the ffi/ module and are wrapped in safe abstractions. Invariant: no unsafe code escapes ffi/ — not even in runtime/ or concurrency_contexts/.

UT: [Contract C046 — State Ownership & Snapshots] Verify that the spec documents: (a) Runtime state (ClientState, AccountEntry, CallEntry) is owned by the reactor thread, (b) read-only snapshots are obtained via read().await on a tokio::sync::RwLock, (c) mutation happens only through RuntimeCommand dispatch.

testExceptions:
- [Item] Actual multi-threaded execution verification (PJSIP callback concurrency)
  - [Reason] impossible to test actual PJSUA threading behavior without the PJSUA native library linked (P0-4). PJSUA internal thread creation is a C library side-effect not controllable from test code.
  - [Why this is not a defect] The concurrency model IS testable — but only after PJSUA linking is available. The MPSC channel pattern itself is testable in isolation (Send+Sync compile check). The PJSUA thread creation is an external library behavior, not a design defect; the Rust wrapper cannot control C library internals. Once P0-4 is complete, integration tests can verify the callback→MPSC path end-to-end.
  - [Alternative verification] Documented concurrency model is reviewed against PJSIP documentation for thread safety assumptions. The MPSC serialization pattern is verified via compile-time Send+Sync trait bounds.

- [Item] End-to-end MPSC dispatch loop latency measurement
  - [Reason] not testable without a fully initialized PJSUA instance, which depends on P0-4 (FFI) and P0-5 (runtime). Until those are available, the dispatch loop cannot be instantiated.
  - [Why this is not a defect] Latency characteristics are a runtime behavior, not a spec defect. The unbounded MPSC channel design is independently testable: tokio::sync::mpsc channel semantics (unbounded queue, send/receive) are tested by the tokio crate itself. The spec documents latency expectations; actual measurement is deferred to the runtime integration phase (P0-5).
  - [Alternative verification] The spec documents the expected latency characteristics and the unbounded channel design rationale. Post-P0-5 integration tests will measure actual dispatch latency under load.

- [Item] Real-time audio callback timing guarantees
  - [Reason] impossible to test the RT callback path (PJSIP -> lock-free queue -> AudioMixer) without native audio device initialization, which requires hardware presence and PJSIP media stack (P0-4, P0-8).
  - [Why this is not a defect] The RT boundary contract (lock-free queue, no blocking) is a DESIGN CONSTRAINT that can be verified independently of hardware. Property-based tests on crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue verify push/pop correctness, capacity, and contention behavior. The actual timing guarantee (no allocations, no blocking) is a programming discipline enforced at code review and documented in the spec. The hardware-dependent path is inherently untestable without hardware, which is not a defect.
  - [Alternative verification] The spec documents the lock-free queue type (crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue), capacity, and the prohibition of blocking operations. Property-based tests on ArrayQueue push/pop semantics verify the data structure correctness independently.
acceptanceCriteria: Four execution contexts are documented with their responsibilities
Command serialization via MPSC is specified
Single-reactor scalability tradeoffs are documented

- [Happy path] The spec is reviewed and approved, documenting: (1) four execution contexts with thread model, responsibilities, and communication boundaries; (2) RuntimeCommand enum with all 10 variants and consistent oneshot reply pattern; (3) MPSC channel types (UnboundedSender/UnboundedReceiver); (4) Send+Sync justification; (5) single-reactor scalability ceiling with partitioning conditions. All 7 Contracts (C002, C010, C011, C012, C034, C038, C046) are addressed with testable assertions.

- [Error case] The spec must document the Shutdown-then-use prevention mechanism: a RuntimeCommand sent after Shutdown is rejected with SipErrorKind::RuntimeShutdown. The oneshot::Sender must-not-be-reused invariant is documented (panic on double-send). The spec must state what happens when the reactor thread panics (sender-side drop-only semantics).

- [Edge case] The spec must document the boundary between AudioWorkerTask (async, may .await) and PJSIP RT callback (no blocking, no allocation, no .await). The lock-free queue (crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue) is the only mechanism crossing this boundary. The spec must document the ~30 call ceiling as a deliberate design choice with the trigger conditions for architectural change (100 accounts / 300 calls).

Specification ticket. The RuntimeCommand enum concrete implementation is in Phase P2.

- [Implementation steps] 1) Add `pub mod concurrency_contexts;` to lib.rs. 2) Create `src/concurrency_contexts/mod.rs` re-exporting command_serialization. 3) Replace the stub in command_serialization.rs with the full RuntimeCommand enum, type aliases, and module-level doc comment documenting all four execution contexts. 4) Run `make check-be` to verify compilation. 5) Run `cargo doc` to verify doc generation.
- [Risks] The RuntimeCommand enum references types (ClientConfig, AccountConfig, AccountId, CallId, SipError) that are all stubs in other P0-* tickets. If those stubs are not structurally compatible (e.g., Send is not auto-derived due to raw pointers or non-Send fields), the RuntimeCommand enum will fail to compile as Send. This is a coordination risk across parallel tickets.
- [Caveats] OutgoingCallRequest, HangupReason, and DmtfMethod types are not yet stubbed in any file. They must be defined in their respective tickets (P0-* or P2). The spec should define them minimally as placeholder enums/structs in command_serialization.rs to enable compilation, with [::STUB::] markers pointing to the real definitions.
- [Open items] Whether RuntimeCommand should derive Debug, Clone, or Serialize is not specified. Clone is impossible due to oneshot::Sender (not Clone). Debug is feasible and recommended for error logging. Serialize may be needed if commands cross process boundaries in future.
- [Future improvements] Multiplexed reactor (partitioned by account group) for >300 concurrent calls (RFC §7.1a). A Ping variant for health-checking the reactor thread. A Batch variant for submitting multiple commands atomically.

- [Invariant on error] Even if the reactor thread panics, the MPSC sender side MUST remain usable (drop-only semantics). The Shutdown command MUST be accepted exactly once; subsequent commands MUST be rejected with SipErrorKind::RuntimeShutdown. The oneshot::Sender MUST NOT be used after sending (documented as a programming error that panics).

The concurrency_contexts/ module MUST NOT import from runtime/, ffi/, or audio/. The RuntimeCommand enum and its dependency types (ClientConfig, AccountConfig, AccountId, CallId, OutgoingCallRequest, HangupReason, DtmfMethod, SipError) MUST all implement Send.
- [Boundary invariant] The audio RT callback path MUST NOT contain any blocking operation, memory allocation, or .await call — communication MUST be via lock-free queue (crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue) only. The reactor MPSC channel is unbounded; no backpressure mechanism is specified for the initial design because the reactor processes commands faster than the user can submit them under the ~30-call load target.
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] Each RuntimeCommand variant SHOULD be logged on dispatch (info level at runtime module, trace level at command_serialization module) with a structured key-value pair: command = variant_name. The Shutdown command must be logged at warn level to make shutdown events conspicuous in production logs.
- [Metrics] RuntimeCommand dispatch count and latency distribution are relevant once the runtime module (P0-5) is implemented. The spec documents the metric names and labels to use: siprs_command_dispatch_total{command="Initialize"}, siprs_command_latency_seconds{command="MakeCall"}. No metrics infrastructure is added at P0-2; the schema is reserved.
- [Error tracking] Commands that return Err should propagate through the oneshot reply naturally. The spec does not mandate additional error tracking — SipError carries sufficient context. The Shutdown-after-use error (SipErrorKind::RuntimeShutdown) should include the rejected command variant name for debugging.
- [Health check] The reactor thread liveness can be probed via a Ping command variant (not in the current spec — added in future). For now, the spec documents that Drop on the CommandSender side signals reactor termination to the receiver.

tickets.background:
N0001 defines the siprs crate purpose: providing safe async PJSUA access for SIP calling via tokio-native API, limited to audio only. This is the root architectural node.

### Goal
Establish the siprs crate as the voice communication foundation within the zasso ecosystem — a safe, async Rust wrapper around PJSUA (PJSIP) FFI bindings providing a fully asynchronous event-driven SIP client.

### Purpose
Provide Rust consumers (specifically, the zasso Tauri desktop app and AI phone agent) with a tokio-native SIP client API that abstracts away all PJSUA FFI complexity, thread safety concerns, and audio pipeline management. The crate wraps unsafe C calls behind a safe Rust layer and exposes async methods for account management, call control, DTMF, event subscriptions, and audio device configuration.

### Motivation
Existing Rust SIP libraries are either incomplete (no production-ready async wrappers), unsafe (raw FFI without safety layers), or non-existent for the PJSIP ecosystem. The zasso project requires decentralized, self-sovereign voice communication that operates independently of OS-level telephony stacks, integrating with zasso's own identity management and P2P network.

### Constraints
- Audio-only: Video, screen sharing, recording files, and GUI are explicitly excluded.
- PJSIP v2.x: The FFI layer targets PJSIP 2.x. No custom SIP stack.
- MSRV 1.95: Minimum supported Rust version is 1.95 (edition 2021).
- Target OS: Linux, macOS, Windows. No mobile or embedded targets in P0-P2.
- Single-threaded reactor: All PJSUA control API calls go through a single core reactor thread via MPSC command serialization.

Each variant carries typed payload + ReplySender<T>. Implements Send. CommandSender = Sender<RuntimeCommand>, CommandReceiver = Receiver<RuntimeCommand>. ReplySender<T> wraps oneshot send semantics.

Direct pjsua_* calls from outside the reactor are prohibited. Verified by: (1) RuntimeCommand is the only command enum — any new PJSUA operation requires a new variant; (2) new_command_channel() is the only channel factory; (3) CommandSender type alias enforces the channel type at compile time.

EventBus with control: tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<SipEvent> and raw_sip: Option<tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<RawSipMessage>>. Methods: new(control_capacity, raw_sip_capacity), subscribe_control(), subscribe_raw_sip(), publish(SipEvent), publish_raw_sip(RawSipMessage). Only events matching the receiver's account_id are returned to the caller. Verified by: multi-account publish test where two receivers for different accounts each receive only their own events.

(2) RawSIP dedicated bus when enabled via RawSipEventConfig::enabled. (3) No raw_sip channel allocation when disabled (Option<Sender> is None). tickets.background:
### Goal
Define the RuntimeCommand enum (10 variants with one-shot reply channels) as the sole dispatch mechanism for PJSUA operations, and implement the EventBus with split control/raw_sip broadcast channels for observable event delivery.

### Purpose
The RuntimeCommand enum enables thread-safe PJSUA command dispatch by serializing all operations through an unbounded MPSC channel, isolating consumers from PJSUA thread-safety constraints. The EventBus provides a loss-tolerant observation mechanism for UI updates and logging, with a dedicated raw_sip bus that prevents high-volume SIP message events from overwhelming control event delivery.

### Motivation
Without RuntimeCommand, every PJSUA call would expose unsafe thread-safety constraints to the consumer, violating the crate design goal of safe async-first SIP communication. Without EventBus, consumers would have no structured way to observe registration state changes, call lifecycle events, or raw SIP message traffic. The split-bus design (C021/N0020) is motivated by the requirement that raw SIP message volume must not cause control event loss.

### Constraints
(1) No tokio runtime yet — std::sync::mpsc provides the MPSC foundation (upgraded to tokio::sync::mpsc in P2 when tokio is added as crate dependency). (2) Placeholder types for SipError, AccountId, CallId, ClientConfig, AccountConfig until downstream P0-* tickets define them. (3) EventBus depends on tokio::sync::broadcast — tokio must be added as a crate dependency during this ticket implementation. (4) SipEventPayload variant payload structs reference downstream types — variants exist as skeletons with unit-like placeholders. (5) No PJSIP FFI bindings exist yet — RuntimeCommand is purely an in-process command enum, not an FFI boundary type.
scope: RuntimeCommand enum with all 10 variants (Initialize, AddAccount, RemoveAccount, SetRegistration, MakeCall, Hangup, Hold, Unhold, SendDtmf, Shutdown)
EventBus with dual control/raw_sip channels via tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender, with subscribe_control/subscribe_raw_sip/publish/publish_raw_sip methods
AccountEventReceiver with account_id filter in recv() loop
Split bus rationale: raw_sip channel is Option<Sender> — None when disabled, zero allocation overhead

**Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**
  - src/concurrency_contexts/command_serialization.rs — modify: update ReplySender to use tokio::sync::oneshot once tokio is added; keep std::sync::mpsc types until P2 tokio upgrade
  - src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs — NEW IMPLEMENTATION: define SipEventPayload enum (40+ variants, #[non_exhaustive]), SipEvent wrapper, EventMeta struct, EventTimestamp type alias
  - src/api/eventbus_receiver.rs — NEW IMPLEMENTATION: define EventBus struct (control: broadcast::Sender<SipEvent>, raw_sip: Option<broadcast::Sender<RawSipMessage>>) with new/subscribe_control/subscribe_raw_sip/publish/publish_raw_sip methods; define AccountEventReceiver with account_id filter loop
  - src/api/mod.rs — add pub mod eventbus_receiver; pub mod event_model_payload_bus declarations if not already present
  - Cargo.toml — add tokio = { version = "1", features = ["sync"] } as dependency
  - Before → After: Two stub files (pub trait Service {} only) become fully implemented types. command_serialization.rs keeps existing structure but uses placeholders that are sys::mpsc-based until P2.
  - API contract: RuntimeCommand enum is pub(crate) — internal API. EventBus, AccountEventReceiver, SipEvent, SipEventPayload become pub re-exported via crate root (N0011) in downstream tickets.
  - Data schema: No persistent schema. EventMeta uses u64 EventTimestamp (ms since epoch). RuntimeCommand variant fields use placeholder types (AccountId=u32, CallId=u32, etc.).
  - Config/env: No new config values. EventBus capacities are constructor parameters.
  - Dependency: tokio (sync feature) added to Cargo.toml.

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - PJSIP FFI bindings — excluded because RuntimeCommand is an in-process command enum; FFI bindings belong to ffi/ module (P1-0+)
  - Reactor implementation — excluded because command dispatch logic is in P1-1 (Reactor). P0-4 defines the command enum and event bus only.
  - tokio::runtime — excluded because EventBus only needs tokio::sync::broadcast which does not require a runtime. RuntimeCommand uses std::sync::mpsc until P2.
  - serde Serialize/Deserialize on EventBus types — deferred to P0-7 (Observability & Capabilities) when serde feature is enabled.

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - Reactor module (P1-1) — direct consumer of RuntimeCommand via MPSC and publisher of SipEvent to EventBus. Impact: new type dependencies; response: P1-1 must import both types.
  - SipClient public API (N0011/P0-5) — exposes EventBus indirectly via subscribe/subscribe_raw_sip/subscribe_account methods. Impact: event bus types become part of public API surface; response: re-export EventBus and SipEvent from crate root.
  - NativeEvent conversion (N0021) — produces SipEventPayload and publishes to EventBus. Impact: must construct correct SipEventPayload variants; response: import event_model_payload_bus types.

tickets.background:
### Goal
P0-6 の目標は、PJSIP callback から受信した NativeEvent を siprs crate の公開イベント型 SipEventPayload に変換する完全なマッピングを実装することである。これにより Reactor は NativeEvent の種類に応じて適切な SipEventPayload を EventBus に publish できるようになる。

### Purpose
NativeEvent から SipEventPayload への変換は siprs crate のイベント駆動アーキテクチャの中核をなす。PJSIP のネイティブイベント表現（pjsip_inv_state, pjsua_call_media_status 等）を crate の公開 API 型に変換することで、下流のコンシューマ（Tauri プラグイン等）は PJSIP の内部表現から独立した一貫したイベントモデルを利用できる。

### Motivation
現在 src/state/ 以下の該当 3 ファイル（m20_native_event_conv.rs, m20_callstate_mapping.rs, m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs）は全て pub enum State {} のスタブ状態であり、変換ロジックが一切実装されていない。これは P0-4 (EventBus) と P0-5 (SipError) が完了した今、次の必須 P0 チケットとしての実装が必要である。

### Constraints
1) NativeEvent enum 自体がコードベースのどこにも定義されていない — P0-6 内で NativeEvent enum を新規定義する。2) PJSIP の pjsip_inv_state や pjsua_call_media_status の FFI 定数は未定義 — 本チケットでは Rust の整数値として受け取り、後続の FFI チケットで実際の PJSIP 定数に置き換える前提とする。3) AccountId/CallId は u32 の type alias（P0-3 のプレースホルダ）を使用。4) MockBackend 未実装のため RegistrationStateChanged の完全な結合テストは実行不可

tickets.background:
N0029 specifies DtmfSentInfo struct and two-phase semantics: send_dtmf() return value = command accepted by PJSIP, DtmfSent event = actual send completed or timeout at 500ms fallback.

### Goal
Define DtmfSentInfo struct, SentDtmfError enum, and DtmfConfig DtmfSent-related fields; implement two-phase send semantics as PJSIP command acceptance (synchronous return) vs send completion event (async DtmfSent).

### Purpose
The two-phase design prevents callers from mistakenly treating send_dtmf() return as "DTMF delivered to peer." The synchronous return confirms local acceptance only; the DtmfSent event confirms actual network send (or timeout). This separation mirrors PJSIP own async callback model.

### Motivation
P0-7 is required before P8-1 (AudioWorker) can implement DTMF sending on the reactor. Current codebase has SipEventPayload::DtmfSent as a unit variant and RuntimeCommand::SendDtmf with method:() — both need concrete types.

### Constraints
- pj_status_t is a PJSIP FFI type; defined as type alias u32 in this phase (FFI crate not yet available).
- ClientConfig is stub-only (P0-1) — DtmfConfig defined standalone; integration deferred.
- DtmfMethod is shared with dtmf_spec_received.rs (N0028) to avoid duplication — single definition.

tickets.background:
N0034 specifies AudioWorkerTask driving mechanism and audio source lifecycle APIs (add/remove/set_gain/mute). N0038 defines Dual Client PJSIP callback routing with single Reactor + EventBus split and account_id-based event dispatch.

### Goal
Specify the architecture and contracts for (1) AudioWorkerTask driving mechanism with AsyncAudioSource lifecycle management (add/remove/set_gain/mute) per N0034, and (2) Dual Client PJSIP callback routing with single Reactor + EventBus split per N0038. Produce spec documents that P0-9 (AudioWorkerTask) and P0-10 (Dual Client Reactor) can implement against.

### Purpose
These two subsystems form the foundation of zasso's voice communication architecture. The AudioWorkerTask bridges the gap between async Rust audio sources (user code running on tokio) and the PJSIP real-time audio callback (C-level lock-free queue boundary). The Dual Client routing enables integration testing with multiple independent SipClients sharing a single PjsuaBackend — a requirement imposed by PJSIP's singleton initialization constraint (pjsua_init() can be called only once). Without Dual Client routing, tests requiring two SipClients would be impossible without modifying PJSIP itself.

### Motivation
Both specifications are gate dependencies for downstream implementation work. Audio mixing (P3-3), IN/OUT pair alignment (N0035), resampling (N0036), and media bridge (N0049) all depend on the AudioWorkerTask frame processing design. Dual Client routing is required for P0-10 (Reactor integration) which in turn enables P5-3 (PJSIP Callback Implementation). The current codebase has all event types and error types defined (P0-4 through P0-7) but no audio pipeline or multi-client orchestration yet — P0-8 bridges that gap with concrete specifications.

### Constraints
(1) PJSIP singleton constraint: pjsua_init() can be called exactly once per process. The PjsuaBackend must use OnceLock or similar. (2) RT boundary: AudioWorkerTask runs on tokio blocking pool, never on PJSIP's real-time callback thread. The only cross-boundary communication is the lock-free queue. (3) No new dependencies on audio libraries — mixing is done via pure Rust (saturating i16 arithmetic). (4) Audio source lifecycle mutations must be frame-boundary-safe (RwLock pattern). (5) The global_runtime() pattern from P0-3 must remain unchanged — single Reactor for all clients.
scope: AudioWorkerTask periodic frame processing. Worker: AudioWorker struct with process_frame() async fn. Mixer reference: Arc<AudioMixer>. Frame boundary: Sources snapshot at start, saturating i16 mix, push to out_queue.

Source lifecycle: add_audio_source(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>) → Result<SourceHandle, SipError>. remove_audio_source(SourceHandle) → Result<(), SipError>. set_gain(SourceHandle, f64) → Result<(), SipError>. mute(SourceHandle, bool) → Result<(), SipError>. All gated by RwLock for frame-boundary safety.

Dual Client: single Reactor + EventBus split. Reactor stores HashMap<AccountId, EventBus> for per-client dispatch. Default EventBus is first SipClient's bus. dispatch_event logic: Some(aid) in map → publish to that bus; Some(aid) not in map → fallback to default; None → publish to default + all client buses.
Account_id-based event dispatch. The Reactor::dispatch_event receives SipEvent (which carries Option<AccountId> in EventMeta) and routes to the correct EventBus per the dispatch logic above.

Source CRUD APIs specified: add_audio_source(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>) → Result<SourceHandle, SipError>, remove_audio_source(SourceHandle) → Result<(), SipError>, set_gain(SourceHandle, f64) → Result<(), SipError>, mute(SourceHandle, bool) → Result<(), SipError>. Each API's precondition/postcondition/invariant is documented. Error conditions map to existing SipErrorKind variants.

Dual Client event routing specified: Reactor stores HashMap<AccountId, EventBus> for per-client dispatch. dispatch_event rules: Some(aid) matching a bus → publish to that bus; Some(aid) not matching → default_event_bus fallback; None → publish to default + all client buses. Single Reactor invariant documented. Test pattern for Dual SipClient initialization documented.

[Happy path] A developer reading the P0-8 spec can implement AudioWorkerTask and Dual Client reactor routing in P0-9 and P0-10 respectively, without needing to re-read RFC nodes N0034 or N0038. All type signatures, error mappings, concurrency semantics, test contracts, and edge cases are covered in this specification.

[Error case] Invalid operations (remove non-existent source, set gain out of range, enqueue native event before reactor init) produce SipError with appropriate SipErrorKind (NotFound, InvalidConfig, NotInitialized). No panics. All error paths are documented and testable.

[Edge case] AudioWorker with zero sources produces silent frames (not an error). process_frame continues even if one source returns an error (best-effort). DualClient with unrecognized account_id falls back silently without logging a warning-level event. frame_duration=0 is rejected at construction.
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) P0-9 (AudioWorkerTask): Implement AudioMixer + AudioWorker + process_frame + source lifecycle API + mix_i16_frame(). New audio/ module. Add crossbeam and slab deps. (2) P0-10 (Dual Client Reactor): Implement Reactor with client_event_buses HashMap, dispatch_event routing logic, default EventBus tracking. Integrate with existing RuntimeCommand enum. (3) P0-9 depends on N0032 (AsyncAudioSource trait) and N0030 (AudioFormat). These are currently stubs — their concrete implementation is a prerequisite. (4) P5-3 (PJSIP Callback Implementation) depends on P0-10 reactor for event routing.
- [Risks] (1) AudioWorker on tokio blocking pool may cause pool exhaustion with 30+ concurrent workers. Mitigation: Use dedicated std::thread if blocking pool proves insufficient. (2) crossbeam::ArrayQueue is fixed-capacity; overflow silently drops frames. Mitigation: Monitor queue occupancy via health metrics; size should be 2-3 frame periods. (3) Slab compaction after source removal may cause fragmentation. Mitigation: Monitor Slab::len() vs capacity and log when fragmentation exceeds threshold. (4) DualClient HashMap lookup latency on critical path. Mitigation: AccountId is u32 — HashMap is O(1); acceptable.
- [Caveats] (1) The AudioWorker does NOT interface with the PJSIP conference bridge directly — that is the responsibility of N0049 (Media Bridge & PJSUA Conference Port, P3-3+). This spec covers the worker → out_queue path only. (2) The DualClient dispatch_event does NOT define how enqueue_native_event is called from PJSIP callbacks — that is P5-3's responsibility. This spec covers the routing (Reactor side) only. (3) SourceHandle is defined as a newtype over u32 (Slab key). It must not be confused with AccountId or CallId.
- [Open items] (1) Detailed AudioFormat struct fields (sample_rate: u32, channels: u8, frame_samples: usize) — defined by N0030 (P0-8 prerequisite but currently a stub). P0-9 implementation may need to define a minimal AudioFormat locally. (2) mix_i16_frame() algorithm: i32 accumulation with saturating_cast to i16. Need to define overflow behavior precisely (clamp vs wrap). RFC §24.3 specifies saturating. (3) Slab vs alternative (Vec with tombstone, generational arena) — Slab chosen for O(1) insert/delete and contiguous iteration. Revisit if fragmentation becomes problematic.
- [Future improvements] (1) Slab-based source storage with generational indices (prevent use-after-free on SourceHandle). (2) AudioWorker priority scheduling (VoIP frames prioritized over non-real-time sources). (3) DualClient reactor scalability: partitioning by account group for >300 concurrent calls. (4) Configurable frame_duration per AudioMixer (currently fixed at construction).

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] (1) AudioMixer must have at least one registered AsyncAudioSource before process_frame produces non-silent output. (2) AudioWorker must be constructed with frame_duration > 0. (3) DualClient Reactor must have at least the default_event_bus initialized. (4) SourceHandle values must be valid Slab keys (non-zero, within capacity).
- [Error invariant] (1) Even if process_frame encounters errors from individual AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk(), the mixed output frame is best-effort: available sources' frames are mixed, absent sources are skipped. (2) DualClient dispatch_event must never panic regardless of account_id value. Unknown account_ids silently fall back to default_event_bus. (3) out_queue overflow on the lock-free queue never causes data corruption — it silently drops oldest (lossy by design, matching EventBus guarantees).
- [Internal state invariant] (1) AudioMixer.sources is always behind RwLock — concurrent reads (process_frame) and writes (add/remove) are safe. (2) SourceEntry fields: source (Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>), gain (f64, always clamped to [0.0, 1.0] or defaulting to 1.0), muted (bool). (3) AudioWorker.mixer reference is Arc<AudioMixer> — shared ownership between worker and audio API layer. (4) DualClient Reactor.client_event_buses is a HashMap<AccountId, EventBus>. The default_event_bus entry is never removed.
- [Boundary invariant] (1) AudioMixer source capacity is bounded by Slab's capacity (default 32 or configurable). Adding beyond capacity returns SipError::InvalidState. (2) process_frame output buffer size = frame_samples = sample_rate * channels * frame_duration_secs. (3) set_gain accepts f64 in [0.0, 1.0]. Values outside this range are clamped. (4) frame_duration must be ≥ 1ms and ≤ 100ms. Values outside this range are rejected at AudioWorker construction.

tickets.investigation:
Code investigation findings for P0-8 (AudioWorkerTask & Dual Client Specification):

## AudioWorkerTask (N0034) — Investigation
**No existing audio/ module**: The audio/ module is not declared in lib.rs. All audio-related files are stubs: asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs (N0032, §23 AsyncAudioSource Trait), audio_format_chunkpair.rs (N0030, §21 Audio Format & AudioChunkPair), audio_subscribe_bp.rs (N0031, §22 Audio Subscribe API). These must be implemented before or concurrently with P0-9.

**RFC §24.3 (N0034) provides concrete pseudocode**: The RFC already specifies AudioWorker struct, process_frame() async function, source loop with .await pull, mix_i16_frame with i32 accumulation → saturating i16, and out_queue push. The spec can reference this directly.

**Reusable types from existing code**:
- SipError (error_design_siperror.rs) — AudioPipelineBroken, AudioFormatUnsupported, NotFound, InvalidConfig variants are already defined.
- RuntimeCommand (command_serialization.rs) — Can be extended with AddAudioSource/RemoveAudioSource/etc. variants in P0-9.
- AccountId (u32 alias), CallId (u32 alias) — Placeholder newtypes; AudioWorker uses CallId.
- Message types: SipEventPayload has MediaActive, MediaStopped, MediaError variants already defined.

## Dual Client (N0038) — Investigation
**No existing runtime/ module**: runtime/ is not declared in lib.rs. The Reactor does not exist yet.

**RFC §27 (N0038) provides concrete architecture**: Single Reactor + EventBus split with account_id-based dispatch. The dispatch_event pseudocode in the RFC is directly implementable.

**Reusable types from existing code**:
- EventBus (eventbus_receiver.rs) — Dual broadcast channel, clone, publish, subscribe. Already supports the per-client bus pattern.
- AccountEventReceiver (eventbus_receiver.rs) — Per-account event filter using account_id. Can be used for per-client event filtering.
- NativeEvent (m20_native_event_conv.rs) — PJSIP callback representation. Reactor::enqueue_native_event converts NativeEvent → SipEventPayload.
- SipEvent, EventMeta (event_model_payload_bus.rs) — EventMeta carries Optional<AccountId> which is the routing key.
- convert_native_event_to_payload (m20_native_event_conv.rs) — Maps NativeEvent to SipEventPayload.

**Existing dual client test stub**: tests/m20_test_dual_client.rs contains only a skeleton. The Dual Client initialization pattern from RFC §27 provides the test pattern structure.

## Key gaps found in investigation:
1. no synchronization primitives beyond std::sync::Mutex in Cargo.toml — crossbeam (ArrayQueue) and slab not yet added
2. SourceHandle type does not exist as a newtype (must be created in P0-9)
3. AudioFormat struct does not exist (defined in N0030 which is a stub)
4. AsyncAudioSource trait does not exist (defined in N0032 which is a stub)
5. global_runtime() function does not exist — placeholder for future OnceLock<Reactor>
6. The existing tests/lib.rs already has 3 test files in src/tests/ (all stubs)

tickets.title: Codec, SRTP, Transport & Shutdown Policies

contracts.precondition: CallMediaPreferences::preferred_codecs may be empty (auto mode) or contain 1+ Codec entries (explicit mode). The SIP client must be initialized and codecs enumerable via enumerate_codecs().
contracts.postcondition: When preferred_codecs is empty: configure_codecs() sets Opus/48000/2ch priority=255, PCMU/8000/1 priority=254, all others priority=0. When preferred_codecs is non-empty: auto mode is bypassed, user-specified codecs are used in SDP offer/answer without priority modification.
contracts.invariant: Opus always gets the highest priority (255) in auto mode. PCMU always gets the second-highest (254). All other codecs get 0 (disabled). Priority values are in u8 range [0, 255]. Non-PCMU/non-Opus codec IDs are never assigned a value > 0.

contracts.precondition: TransportConfig enum (UDP/TCP/TLS) and TlsConfig struct are defined in src/config/transport_ice_spec.rs (N0015). Feature flags tls and srtp are declared in Cargo.toml.
contracts.postcondition: SrtpPolicy enum (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory) is defined and feature-gated with #[cfg(feature = "srtp")]. ReconnectPolicy struct defines per-protocol reconnection strategy (UDP, TCP, TLS). Transport validation rejects Mandatory+Optional when srtp feature is disabled.
contracts.invariant: SRTP feature gate is active: when cfg(feature = "srtp") is false, SrtpPolicy::Mandatory and SrtpPolicy::Optional are either compile-time unavailable or rejected at config validation. SrtpPolicy::Disabled is always available regardless of feature flag.

contracts.precondition: Shutdown sequence is defined (N0043, src/state/shutdown_specification.rs). is_shutting_down flag is accessible by the dispatch function. RuntimeCommand enum includes GetAccountInfo (from N0010, P0-6) and will include ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect (from P0-8 AudioWorkerTask).
contracts.postcondition: When is_shutting_down=true: GetAccountInfo variants pass through to execute_get_account_info() (read-only permitted). ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect variants return Err(SipError::invalid_state("shutting down")). All other RuntimeCommand variants return Err(SipError::invalid_state("shutting down")) via catch-all. When is_shutting_down=false: normal dispatch proceeds unchanged.
contracts.invariant: GetAccountInfo is always permitted during shutdown (read-only invariant). ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect are always rejected during shutdown. No RuntimeCommand variant causes a panic during shutdown dispatch. The dispatch decision is deterministic based solely on is_shutting_down and the command variant.

tickets.background:
N0041 defines two-layer codec: explicit user specification vs auto mode (Opus=255, PCMU=254). N0042 defines SrtpPolicy (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory), transport reconnection per protocol, ReconnectPolicy. N0044 specifies shutdown command routing: GetAccountInfo permitted (read-only), ConfConnect/Disconnect rejected.

### Goal
Implement the M20 policy layer for codec auto-mode (N0041), SRTP + transport reconnection (N0042), and shutdown command routing (N0044) as specified by the RFC graph §29-32. Each policy must be self-contained within its target file and fully testable.

### Purpose
Provide the runtime policy configuration that governs how siprs handles codec selection (auto vs explicit), media security (SRTP on/off/optional), transport resilience (reconnection per protocol), and safe shutdown behavior (read-only commands permitted, mutating commands rejected). These policies complete the M20 extension to the config and error subsystems.

### Motivation
M20 RFC sections §29-32 define the policy layer that bridges static configuration (P0-1/P0-2) and dynamic runtime behavior (P0-7/P0-8). Without these policies, the reactor would lack the decision logic for codec priority ordering, SRTP enforcement, transport failover strategy, and graceful command rejection during shutdown.

### Constraints
- FFI crate (P0-9) is not yet available: codec priority setting via pjsua_codec_set_priority must use a mockable/injectable wrapper.
- ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect RuntimeCommand variants are added by P0-8 (AudioWorkerTask) — P1-1 shutdown routing depends on those variants existing.
- TransportConfig types (UdpTransportConfig, TcpTransportConfig, TlsTransportConfig) are defined in N0015 (P0-1). ReconnectPolicy must be compatible with those types.
- SRTP feature flag (cfg(feature = "srtp")) must be declared in Cargo.toml before implementation.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- [Boy Scout — Translatability Plan]

  ## 1. extract_codec_priority() from inline match
  RFC §29 contains an inline match block for codec priority assignment. Extract into a named function
  `fn codec_priority_for_id(codec_id: &str) -> Option<u8>` that returns Some(255)/Some(254)/Some(0)/None
  for unknown. This makes the dispatch logic translatable:
    "determine priority for this codec ID → if known, call set_priority → if set fails, return error"

  ## 2. dispatch_command as a pure function
  The shutdown routing match block should be extracted as a pure function:
  `fn should_allow_during_shutdown(cmd: &RuntimeCommand) -> Result<(), SipError>`
  This separates the decision logic from the reactor loop, making it testable and translatable:
    "if shutting down, match command → GetAccountInfo OK, ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect rejected, all else rejected"

  ## 3. Named constants for priority values
  Replace magic numbers 255, 254, 0 with:
    pub(crate) const CODEC_PRIORITY_OPUS: u8 = 255;
    pub(crate) const CODEC_PRIORITY_PCMU: u8 = 254;
    pub(crate) const CODEC_PRIORITY_DISABLED: u8 = 0;

  ## 4. ReconnectPolicy as a struct with named fields, not a tuple
  ReconnectPolicy should be a struct with named fields (udp_retry: RetryConfig, tcp_retry: RetryConfig, tls_retry: RetryConfig) so that
  construction reads as "ReconnectPolicy { udp_retry: RetryConfig::default(), tcp_retry: ..., tls_retry: ... }"
  rather than a positional tuple.

  ## 5. Clean up stub artifacts
  Replace pub struct Config {} and pub enum Error {} stubs in all three target files with real implementations.
  Add #[::STUB::] markers only for parts that genuinely depend on future tickets (FFI calls, runtime integration).

  ## 6. Code outside scope
  N0040 (codec_policy_fallback.rs) and N0015 (transport_ice_spec.rs) and N0043 (shutdown_specification.rs) 
  remain stubs — they are not touched by P1-1. This is acceptable as they belong to separate tickets.

tickets.background:
N0046 defines tracing spans, optional metrics counters (active_calls, registered_accounts, etc.), and ClientCapabilities. N0047 specifies SecretString for passwords, Authorization header redaction, TLS verify default true. N0055 documents panic policy: panic-free goal, catch_unwind in FFI callbacks with cleanup procedure.

### Goal
Define and implement the observability types (tracing spans, metrics counters/gauges, ClientCapabilities), security primitives (SecretString, TLS_VERIFY_DEFAULT, authorization header redaction), and panic policy (catch_unwind cleanup procedure) as concrete testable Rust types in the siprs crate.

### Purpose
These three concerns are cross-cutting requirements that every higher-level ticket (P2+) depends on: tracing spans for debugging production issues, metrics for operational monitoring, ClientCapabilities for capability negotiation, SecretString for audit-proof password handling, TLS verify default for secure-by-default transport, catch_unwind for FFI safety.

### Motivation
Current stub implementations (pub struct Config {}, pub fn authorize() {}, pub enum Error {}) block all P2+ tickets that need to consume these types. Without concrete observability types, debugging production issues is impossible. Without SecretString, accidental password leaks in logs are guaranteed. Without catch_unwind cleanup, a panic in a PJSUA callback leaks native resources.

### Constraints
- No `tracing`, `secrecy`, `zeroize` crates in Cargo.toml yet — must add dependencies as needed
- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in lib.rs — all zeroization must use safe crate abstractions (zeroize crate) not manual unsafe
- Feature flag discipline: metrics behind #[cfg(feature = "metrics")], serde behind existing #[cfg(feature = "serde")]
- Existing test patterns: #[cfg(test)] mod tests with Result<(), String> return type

tickets.title: Usage Examples & Code Samples

contracts.precondition: Usage needs documentation — each usage scenario (client init, account, call, audio tap, TTS) must have a corresponding compilable example file under examples/
contracts.postcondition: Device policy and usage examples provided — all 5 example categories produce compilable Rust files and the examples/ directory contains a README.md explaining each example

tickets.background:
N0050 provides complete usage examples: client initialization, account add/register, make call with events, audio tap with WAV export, and AI TTS source insertion.

### Goal
Produce 5 compilable Rust example files under examples/ demonstrating all major crate capabilities: client init, account management, call flow, audio tap, and custom audio source injection. Each example must compile via cargo check and serve as both documentation and a compile-time regression test for the public API.

### Purpose
Usage examples bridge the gap between API reference docs and real-world integration. They answer the question "how do I use this crate?" without requiring downstream developers to reverse-engineer the module structure. They also serve as compile-time integration tests — if the public API changes in a breaking way, the examples fail to compile.

### Motivation
Without compilable examples, downstream consumers must infer usage patterns from type signatures and test code. This creates a high barrier to adoption and risks incorrect usage. The RFC §41 specifies concrete usage patterns that must be reflected in actual code. Publishing examples at the same time as the initial API stabilization (P1) ensures the API is actually usable from an external perspective before v0.1.0 release.

### Constraints
(1) Examples cannot execute in CI because PJSIP native library is not available — verification is limited to cargo check (compilation only). (2) Examples must compile without pjsua-sys or any feature that requires the native PJSIP library. (3) Examples use the planned public API surface types (SipClient, ClientConfig, AccountConfig, EventBus, AudioTapHandle, AsyncAudioSource) which are implemented across P0-3 through P1-2. (4) The cpal-input feature is optional — microphone-related code must be feature-gated. (5) Examples must not call .unwrap() in production code paths, following the crate's ?-propagation standard.

testExceptions:
[Item] Full runtime execution of examples with real PJSIP library — impossible to test in CI.
[Reason] PJSIP is a native C library requiring platform-specific installation. CI environment does not include PJSIP development libraries.
[Justification] This is not a defect — FFI-bound crates standardly verify via compilation-only checks. The crate architecture separates public API from FFI bindings. cargo check --examples proves all type-level correctness without the native library.
[Alternative verification] cargo check --examples provides full type-checking of all example code paths.

[Item] Audio tap example with real audio device (microphone) I/O — not testable in CI without audio hardware.
[Reason] CI runners have no audio hardware. The open_default_microphone_source function requires a physical or virtual audio device.
[Justification] This is not a defect — microphone support is optional via the cpal-input feature flag (§40). The example uses #[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")] gating, proving the design handles both states correctly. The non-microphone path (WAV output) is always compilable.
[Alternative verification] Compilation with --features cpal-input checks the feature-gated path. Compilation without the feature checks the fallback path.

[Item] Network-dependent registration and call scenarios — cannot test without live SIP server.
[Reason] Registration and call examples require a running SIP server/PBX (e.g., sip:pbx.example.com). CI has no SIP infrastructure.
[Justification] This is not an architectural defect — network-dependent testing is intentionally separated into Layer 2-4 of the test strategy (§43). Examples are static documentation verifying API type-correctness at compile time. The async method signatures (returning Result<T, SipError>) make network errors first-class without requiring a live network.
[Alternative verification] Compilation verifies type correctness of the entire call chain using ? propagation from SipClient async methods.

The main function must follow the standard Rust example convention: pub fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> or async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>.
- [Error invariant] All example code must propagate errors via the ? operator — no unwrap(), expect(), or panic!() in production logic paths. The sole exception is the #[tokio::main] attribute macro return type requirement. If an error occurs at any point in the example flow, the entire example must terminate gracefully via returned Err.
- [Internal state invariant] Examples must reference only public API items (pub items re-exported from lib.rs). Internal modules (config/, api/, state/, error/, concurrency_contexts/) must not be imported directly. This guarantees that example files document only the intended public surface.
- [Boundary invariant] Feature-flagged functionality must be wrapped in #[cfg(feature = "...")] attributes. The default features build (serde + tls) must not fail due to missing microphone/cpal functionality. The srtp feature must not leak into example code when srtp is disabled.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- [examples/ directory] This ticket creates the examples/ directory and 5 .rs files + 1 README.md. There is no existing code to refactor — all files are net-new. However, the following translatability principles will be applied to the new example code:

1. **Function names as verb phrases**: Each example uses a single async main() function whose sequence of calls reads as a narrative: `create_client()`, then `add_account()`, then `make_call()`, then `receive_events()`. Internal helper functions use verb phrases like `pair_to_stereo_i16()`.

2. **Variable names as domain concepts**: Use `client`, `account`, `call_id`, `audio_tap`, `source_id` rather than `c`, `a`, `cid`, `tap`, `src`. Configuration structs use their type-level field names.

3. **One function one responsibility**: Each example demonstrates exactly one crate capability. The event processing loop uses match expressions that read as exhaustive case analysis rather than a monolithic handler.

4. **Hardcoded values as named constants**: User-facing constants (port numbers, example URIs, STUN server addresses) are defined as `const` at the top of each example file rather than inlined.

5. **No error swallowing**: All `Result` values are propagated with `?`. Comments document what each error means in the example context.

tickets.title: Test Strategy & CI/CD Pipeline

contracts.precondition: §5 Functional Requirements define a normative scope; each requirement must be testable via at least one of the 4 test layers. New requirements must be assigned to a layer (1-4) at specification time.
contracts.postcondition: The 4-layer test strategy document (test_strategy_4layer.rs) defines distinct scopes, tools, environments, and verification targets for each layer — Unit (MockBackend, PJSIP-free), State-Machine (MockBackend+Runtime), SIP Integration (Docker Asterisk/FreeSWITCH), Interop (real PBX/Proxy).
contracts.invariant: Each layer has mutually exclusive scope: Layer 1 = pure logic (no async, no networking), Layer 2 = async state machines (MockBackend), Layer 3 = Dockered SIP protocol tests, Layer 4 = production PBX interop. No layer duplicates another layer's test coverage domain.

contracts.precondition: 4-layer test strategy with defined layer scopes (C053-postcondition) is established as the framework for M20 feature mapping.
contracts.postcondition: Each of the 11 M20 features (NativeEvent conversion, RegistrationStateChanged, CallStateChanged pjsip_inv_state, CallMediaStateChanged, DtmfSent dual-path, DtmfSent timeout fallback, SubscribeAudio conf_connect, conf_connect/disconnect RuntimeCommand, configure_codecs auto mode, Dual Client call_reject, low-priority NativeEvent) is assigned to a specific test layer with concrete verification criteria and documented resolution conditions for placeholders.
contracts.invariant: DualClientContext provides 2 SipClient instances (client_a/client_b) sharing the same PjsuaBackend singleton with separate EventBus instances, using separate accounts (account_a/account_b) for bidirectional call testing.

contracts.precondition: Build strategy (§28 N0039) defining OS-specific dependency resolution (prebuilt vs source build) and target platform capabilities (macOS: CoreAudio/Security framework, Linux: ALSA/OpenSSL, Windows: WinMM) is established.
contracts.postcondition: CI/CD pipeline specified as GitHub Actions workflow with: (1) matrix build across windows-latest, macos-14, ubuntu-22.04 with feature combinations default/tls/srtp/tls+srtp; (2) Docker Asterisk integration test job; (3) macOS prebuilt refresh pipeline.
contracts.invariant: CI matrix covers exactly 3 operating systems (windows-latest, macos-14, ubuntu-22.04) and 4 feature combinations (default, tls, srtp, tls+srtp) = 12 total configurations. Prebuilt refresh runs only on macos-14. Docker integration runs only on ubuntu-22.04.

contracts.precondition: Core test strategy (Layers 1-4 as defined in C053-postcondition) is established and covers the normative functional scope.
contracts.postcondition: Layer 5 (API Integration) extends the 4-layer strategy with integration tests that validate the crate's public API surface against documented usage patterns.
contracts.invariant: Test directory structure mirrors the src/api/ module layout — each public API module has a corresponding test file in tests/ or src/tests/.

tickets.background:
N0052 defines 4-layer test strategy: Unit (PJSIP-free), State-Machine (MockBackend), SIP Integration (Docker), Interop (real PBX). N0053 maps M20 features to test layers with placeholder resolution conditions. N0054 specifies CI matrix, Docker integration test job, and prebuilt refresh pipeline.

### Goal
Establish a comprehensive 4-layer test strategy and CI/CD pipeline for the siprs crate, ensuring all M20 features have assigned test layers with documented verification criteria, and that the CI pipeline provides automated build/test across all 3 target OSes with Docker-based SIP integration testing and macOS prebuilt refresh automation.

### Purpose
Define a structured testing approach that provides fast developer feedback (Layer 1/2 unit tests, ~seconds) while ensuring real SIP protocol compatibility (Layer 3 Docker tests) and production PBX interoperability (Layer 4). The CI/CD pipeline eliminates manual build steps and ensures every commit is tested against all target platforms.

### Motivation
Current test infrastructure is minimal (stub files only: `test_strategy_4layer.rs`, `m20_test_dual_client.rs`, `cicd_docker_prebuilt.rs` all contain `[::STUB::]` markers). No CI workflows exist. M20 feature implementation (P0-2 through P1-3) has outpaced test infrastructure; without documented test layers, each new feature lacks a defined verification strategy, risking regressions as the codebase grows.

### Constraints
- Must maintain PJSIP-free compilation for fast developer feedback — Layer 1/2 tests cannot depend on pjsua FFI
- Layer 3 tests must be gated behind `#[cfg(feature = "pjsip")]` or `#[ignore]` since they need Docker
- Layer 4 tests are CI-external and must be manual-run; their spec must include runbook steps
- CI matrix limited to GitHub Actions runners (windows-latest, macos-14, ubuntu-22.04) per §28 Build Strategy
- Prebuilt refresh must preserve existing BUILD.md manual instructions as fallback

testExceptions:
**Exception 1: Docker-based SIP integration tests (Layer 3)**
  - Item: Docker Asterisk/FreeSWITCH integration tests are not testable via `cargo test --lib` because they require Docker daemon with port bindings (5060/udp, 5061/tcp), which is only available on ubuntu-22.04 GitHub Actions runner
  - Reason: These tests use actual pjsua library via `--features pjsip` and cannot run without Docker. Core unit tests must remain PJSIP-free for fast `cargo test` feedback (Layer 1 and Layer 2 constraints).
  - Justification: This is not a design defect — the feature is testable in Docker CI environment, just not in `cargo test --lib`. The architectural separation of PJSIP-dependent vs PJSIP-independent tests is intentional. This is a CI environment constraint, not an architectural defect.
  - Alternative verification: The spec document includes complete Docker configuration (image: asterisk:20.6.0, port maps, env vars) and CI job definition. A #[cfg(feature = "pjsip")] gated integration test file verifies the spec document references Docker correctly.

**Exception 2: Layer 4 interop tests with real PBX/Proxy**
  - Item: Interop tests against real Asterisk LTS, FreeSWITCH, OpenSIPS, Kamailio, and 3CX SBC are not testable in CI because they require network access to live infrastructure
  - Reason: These tests require PBX instances with specific configurations (SRTP mandatory on 3CX, TLS transport on OpenSIPS, etc.) that cannot be replicated in ephemeral CI containers.
  - Justification: This is not a design defect — each interaction with each PBX is deterministic and could be tested given the infrastructure. The limitation is purely operational (no live PBX CI runners). This is an environmental constraint, not an architectural defect.
  - Alternative verification: Spec documents P0/P1 priority split with detailed test catalog per PBX (REGISTER, INVITE, BYE, DTMF, SRTP, etc.). Manual test procedures are referenced. Layer 3 Docker tests verify the code paths that Layer 4 will exercise in production.

**Exception 3: Prebuilt PJSIP refresh pipeline end-to-end verification**
  - Item: The full prebuilt refresh pipeline (cmake configure/build on macos-14, artifact upload) is not testable during `make test` because it requires specific macOS toolchain and network access. It is impossible to test within the unit test framework.
  - Reason: cmake build takes 5-10 minutes, requires specific macOS toolchain (Xcode CLT, CMake), and needs network access to upload artifacts.
  - Justification: This is not a design defect — the pipeline execution is fully deterministic and testable in its native environment (GitHub Actions macos-14 runner). The limitation is that `make test` is a different context from CI. This is a build-environment constraint, not an architectural defect.
  - Alternative verification: Spec documents complete cmake configuration flags (-DSRTP_WITH_OPENSSL=OFF, -DPJMEDIA_WITH_VIDEO=OFF, -G "Unix Makefiles"), build steps, and artifact upload configuration. Existing vendor/prebuilt/BUILD.md provides supplementary manual instructions.

tickets.background:
N0013 defines ClientConfig struct with all sub-configs (ClientAudioConfig, TimeoutConfig, RawSipEventConfig, LogLevel) and defaults. N0056 documents memory ownership rules for native callbacks and default policies. N0057 defines lib.rs module declarations and 12 acceptance criteria. N0058 is the RFC closure statement.

### Goal
Define the foundational configuration types (ClientConfig, ClientAudioConfig, TimeoutConfig, RawSipEventConfig, LogLevel) with Default implementations, document the 4 memory ownership rules and 6 default policies for native FFI callbacks, and enumerate the 12 acceptance criteria that verify the crate's completeness.

### Purpose
Establish the single source of truth for SIP client configuration so that all downstream types (AccountConfig, TransportConfig, IceConfig) can depend on a stable ClientConfig interface. Memory ownership rules prevent undefined behavior across the Rust↔PJSIP FFI boundary. Acceptance criteria serve as the master checklist for crate delivery.

### Motivation
ClientConfig is the entry point for every user of the siprs crate — without it no account, transport, call, or audio configuration can be constructed. The FFI memory rules are a prerequisite for any PJSIP binding implementation. The acceptance criteria define what "done" means for the entire crate, enabling parallel ticket execution against a shared target.

### Constraints
1. Audio format types (SampleRate, BitDepth, ChannelLayout, AudioFormat, ResamplerQuality) are defined in P2-2 (audio pipeline) — ClientAudioConfig must reference them as forward-declarations or stubs.
2. TransportConfig, IceConfig, StunServerConfig, TurnServerConfig types are defined in P2-3 — ClientConfig must reference them as type stubs.
3. Memory ownership rules are documentation only (no runtime enforcement code) — they describe contracts for the future ffi module (P0-4+).
4. No external crate dependencies beyond those already declared in Cargo.toml (tokio, thiserror, serde, tracing, cfg-if, zeroize).
