testExceptions:
Exception: P2-1 defines struct types and Default impls only (no runtime logic).
  Reason: It is impossible to test runtime behavior because ClientConfig, ClientAudioConfig, TimeoutConfig, RawSipEventConfig, LogLevel are pure data types with no dynamic logic, branching, or error paths. All observable behavior is verified at compile time via type-checking and include_str! assertions.
  This is not a design defect: Config structs are intentionally designed as value objects — all validation semantics are deferred to the separate validation phase (N0051). Adding dummy validation logic solely for testability would produce a worse architecture.

Exception: Memory ownership rules and default policies are documentation-only.
  Reason: It is impossible to test the FFI memory rules because the FFI module does not yet exist. The 4 rules and 6 default policies are design contracts constraining the future FFI module — they describe how it MUST behave, not how it currently behaves.
  This is not an architectural defect: Documenting design constraints before implementation is the correct order. The rules will be enforced during code review of the FFI module (future ticket). The include_str!() assertions verify the rules are documented without requiring runtime enforcement.

Exception: 12 acceptance criteria from RFC 50 cover system-level behaviors across multiple future tickets.
  Reason: It is impossible to test all 12 acceptance criteria within P2-1 scope — they require a fully assembled SipClient with PJSUA bindings, multi-account registration, DTMF relay, audio pipeline, etc., spanning the entire P2 series plus P3.
  This is not a design defect: The acceptance criteria are deliberately designed as the crate-level delivery checklist. Enumeration in this spec with ticket ownership mapping is the correct approach — each downstream ticket references which criteria it addresses.

**[Happy path] P2-1 implementation is complete when:** cargo build succeeds, all unit tests pass, and all 11 acceptance criteria above are satisfied. ClientConfig::default() returns a fully populated struct whose values match the RFC §10 specification.

**[Error case] No runtime error paths exist for config type definitions:** ClientConfig and its sub-configs are pure data types. The Default implementation is infallible. Field validation is deferred to the N0051 validation phase (separate ticket).

**[Edge case] Type forward-reference compatibility:** ClientAudioConfig references AudioFormat/SampleRate/etc. (P2-2) and ClientConfig references TransportConfig/IceConfig/etc. (P2-3). If these types are not yet defined, P2-1 must compile with stub definitions. If they are later defined, P2-1 must not break. This is verified by the integration tests.

tickets.background:
N0039 defines prebuilt-first then source-build fallback strategy with CMake flags and OS-specific package dependencies. N0066 specifies 0.x flexible versioning and SIP networking (TLS cert management, DNS SRV/NAPTR delegation to PJSIP, multi-network interface).

### Goal
Replace the two [::STUB::] markers in src/build/build_strategy_os_deps.rs (N0039) and src/config/semver_sip_networking.rs (N0066) with documentation-complete implementation files. The build strategy file must document the prebuilt-first → source-build-fallback algorithm, CMake flag configuration, and OS-specific package dependencies for all 3 target platforms. The semver/SIP networking file must document 0.x versioning policy, TLS certificate management via NativeEvent, DNS SRV/NAPTR delegation to PJSIP, and multi-network interface configuration.

### Purpose
Build strategy defines how the siprs crate compiles and links against PJSIP — the critical compile-time dependency for all downstream functionality. Without a documented build strategy, developers cannot set up their development environment, CI cannot validate cross-platform compatibility, and the crate cannot be published to crates.io. Versioning policy provides the community standard (semver) contract for dependents. SIP networking details document TLS security posture and multi-network deployment scenarios that system integrators need.

### Motivation
P2-1 (ClientConfig) is complete. The two stub files (build_strategy_os_deps.rs, semver_sip_networking.rs) are the last remaining P2 targets before P2-3 (TransportConfig/IceConfig) can proceed. The versioning policy (.1) was already established by N0006/P0-1; this ticket expands it to cover 0.x operations and SIP networking details that were out of scope for the initial policy definition. Build strategy documentation is a prerequisite for the CI/CD pipeline (P1-4) matrix validation.

### Constraints
1. Build strategy is documentation-only — actual build.rs implementation (compile-time CMake execution, link directives, bindgen) will be implemented in a later ticket when PJSIP vendor directory exists.
2. Versioning policy (.1) was already defined by P0-1 (versioning_policy.rs). This ticket does NOT modify versioning_policy.rs — it adds semver_sip_networking.rs as a separate extension file.
3. TLS certificate management NativeEvent types are defined in api/ module by P0-4. This ticket documents the data contracts but does not implement NativeEvent parsing.

tickets.background:
N0059 specifies separate siprs-server crate with Axum for HTTP/WS API, dependency direction siprs-server→siprs only. N0060 defines dual-license (MIT/Apache 2.0) with GPL linking exception and multi-instance via PjsuaBackend singleton sharing. N0067 provides I/O boundary reference with 7 observed boundaries.

### Goal
Document the architecture decisions for crate split (siprs + siprs-server), license policy (MIT/Apache 2.0 + GPL linking exception), multi-instance model (PjsuaBackend singleton sharing), Non-Pure Rust FFI audit policy, and 7 I/O boundary reference information (B1-B7) — producing specs/P2-3.md as the primary deliverable.

### Purpose
This ticket serves as the architectural foundation for all HTTP/WS API Layer tickets (P3-3, P4-4, P5-4, P6-3). The crate split decision directly affects Cargo.toml structure, dependency management, build times, and Tauri bundle size. The license policy is a compliance prerequisite for 1.0 release. The I/O boundary reference provides future split guidance based on observed design boundaries.

### Motivation
Crate split motivation: (1) Tauri app embedded use does not need Axum/tokio-tungstenite dependencies — split minimizes bundle size; (2) siprs core tests must be free from HTTP dependency; (3) future backend replacement (PJSIP → custom) must not affect siprs-server. License motivation: PJSIP is GPL v2 — linking exception needed to avoid copyleft contamination of applications using siprs. I/O boundary motivation: RFC §61 documents naturally observed split points for future graphify-rfc refactoring.

### Constraints
(1) siprs Cargo.toml must NOT add axum/tokio-tungstenite/rusqlite/sea-orm even optionally — zero HTTP deps invariant. (2) License is provisional until 1.0 release — current Cargo.toml already states MIT OR Apache-2.0. (3) PjsuaBackend singleton constraint: pjsua_init() is single-call — multi-instance design must share the singleton. (4) I/O boundary document is reference only — not prescriptive split instructions. (5) FFI unsafe code must remain isolated to ffi/ module.

tickets.background:
N0063 specifies JWT token issuance via SIP account auth, Axum JWT auth middleware layer, and AuthConfig defaults (LocalhostOnly for development).

### Goal
Produce specs/P2-4.md documenting the complete JWT Authentication Model design: (1) JWT token issuance endpoint (POST /api/v1/auth/token) with request/response format and SIP credential verification, (2) JWT claims structure (sub, username, domain, exp, scope), (3) AxumJWTAuthLayer middleware and AxumJWTAuthMiddleware architecture, (4) AuthConfig struct with AuthMode enum (LocalhostOnly, ApiKey, Jwt), (5) WebSocket JWT validation strategy.

### Purpose
This spec serves as the design contract for all HTTP/WS API Layer tickets (P3-3, P4-4, P5-4, P6-3) that consume or implement JWT authentication. The JWT auth model constrains (SS55 -> SS54) the HTTP/WS API Protocol — specifying the auth architecture before route implementation prevents integration mismatches. The AuthConfig design contract ensures consistent auth defaults (LocalhostOnly) across all deployment modes.

### Motivation
JWT authentication is required because: (1) SIP accounts need credential-based access to REST/WS APIs without exposing raw SIP credentials on every request, (2) WebSocket connections (audio + control channels) require stateless token validation, (3) the Axum middleware pattern (tower Layer) decouples auth logic from route handlers, (4) development convenience requires LocalhostOnly mode to skip JWT overhead during local debugging, (5) future multi-tenant deployments need ApiKey and Jwt modes.

### Constraints
(1) siprs Cargo.toml must NOT add axum/jsonwebtoken/tokio-tungstenite even optionally — zero HTTP deps invariant. JWT types are design contracts for siprs-server. (2) AuthConfig/AuthMode structs/enums are NOT implemented in this ticket — P3-3 (N0061) implements the config types. (3) No Axum router or middleware implementation in this ticket — P4-4 (N0062) implements routes with middleware. (4) Default auth is LocalhostOnly — external access requires explicit opt-in. (5) The auth_jwt_middleware.rs stub remains a placeholder — this ticket only documents the design.

tickets.background:
N0065 defines Layer 5 for HTTP/WS API integration tests with REST API tests, WebSocket event stream tests, audio binary frame tests, JWT auth flow tests, and SIP combined tests.

### Goal
Define the Layer 5 API Integration Test Infrastructure as a formal specification: document the test directory layout, Axum TestResponse code examples, WebSocket test patterns, JWT auth flow tests, and SIP combined test patterns. This spec serves as the blueprint for future siprs-server crate tests (P3-4+).

### Purpose
Existing Layers 1-4 cover unit/state-machine/SIP/interop testing. Layer 5 fills the gap for HTTP/WS API-level integration tests (REST endpoints, WebSocket event streams, JWT authentication flows, audio binary frames). Without this layer, the full SIP service cannot be validated at the API boundary.

### Motivation
The P2-4 (JWT Auth Model) and P2-3 (Crate Split) tickets define the JWT authentication layer and I/O boundary architecture respectively. Layer 5 is needed now to specify how these will be integration-tested before the siprs-server crate is created (P3-4). Spec-first ensures the test infrastructure design is validated before implementation.

### Constraints
1. siprs core crate MUST NOT have HTTP dependencies (zero HTTP deps invariant enforced by `p2x4_zero_http_deps_invariant`). 2. Layer 5 runtime tests require the future `siprs-server` crate with `axum-test = "20.1.0"`. 3. The spec must follow the pattern established by anthropx crate (`crates/anthropx/src/http/auth.rs`). 4. Test directory layout must follow RFC §57.2: `tests/api/`, `tests/ws/`, `tests/integration/`. 5. Only spec validation tests run in the siprs crate; runtime tests are deferred to P3-4.
scope: REST API unit tests with Axum TestResponse — spec document defines code examples using `axum_test::TestServer` with router setup, request building, and response assertions per anthropx pattern
WebSocket event stream and audio frame tests — spec document defines WebSocket connection pattern via `axum_test::TestServer.ws()` and event stream consumption with `read.next().await`
JWT auth flow tests (token issue → verify → reject) — spec documents test scenarios for JWT token issuance, Bearer token validation, expired token rejection, and WebSocket query-param auth fallback
SIP combined tests (Docker Asterisk + HTTP API) — spec documents combined test scenario structure: Docker Asterisk container + HTTP API calls for end-to-end SIP signaling verification
Graphify/boundify integration notes — spec documents how Layer 5 tests split at I/O boundaries when future RFC graph partitioning occurs

This is not a defect — it is an explicit, intentional design boundary: siprs is the SIP library core, and siprs-server (future P3-4) owns the HTTP layer where these runtime tests will execute. - **`crates/anthropx/src/http/auth.rs`**: Uses `axum_test::TestServer` with builder pattern: `server.get("/path").add_header("authorization", "Bearer valid-token").await`.

### 3. RFC and Spec Structure
- **N0065 (§57)**: Defines 5-layer test architecture extending N0052's 4 layers. Layer 5 includes REST, WebSocket, audio, JWT, SIP combined.
- **RFC §57.2 Directory Layout**: `tests/api/`, `tests/ws/`, `tests/integration/` with specific test files (auth_test.rs, accounts_test.rs, calls_test.rs, health_test.rs, event_stream_test.rs, audio_frame_test.rs, sip_via_api_test.rs).

### 4. Existing Ticket Patterns (P2-1 through P2-4 specs)
- All specs at `specs/P2-*.md` follow a consistent template with TDD header, RFC reference, background, scope, acceptance criteria, invariants, contracts, test plan.
- P2-4 defines JWT claims (`sub`, `username`, `domain`, `exp`, `scope`), auth modes (LocalhostOnly, ApiKey, Jwt), and the middleware pattern.

### 5. Key Architectural Constraints
- **Zero HTTP deps invariant**: siprs core must never import axum, axum-test, or jsonwebtoken.
- **Layer 5 runtime tests deferred**: Run in future `siprs-server` crate (P3-4).
- **TestLayer enum upgrade**: Existing P1-4 tests assume 4 layers and must be updated to 5.

tickets.background:
N0011 defines the complete public API: crate root re-exports, SipClient struct/methods, SipAccountHandle API, OutgoingCallRequest. N0014 defines AccountConfig with codec, DTMF, media policies. N0015 defines TransportConfig (UDP/TCP/TLS), ICE/STUN/TURN configs. These form the public interface of the crate.

### Goal
Define the complete public API surface of the siprs crate — struct definitions, method signatures, type aliases, and re-exports — for `SipClient`, `SipAccountHandle`, `AccountConfig`, `TransportConfig`, and supporting configuration types, enabling users to construct a SIP client, manage accounts, configure transport, and initiate calls.

### Purpose
Establish the single, authoritative public interface (`pub` types and methods) that downstream consumers (zasso desktop app, CLI tools, integration tests) use to interact with the SIP voice communication system. Without this definition, all downstream development is blocked on knowing which types and methods will be available.

### Motivation
P0 through P2 tickets have established the foundational config layer (ClientConfig), concurrency model (RuntimeCommand), error types (SipError), event system (EventBus), and ID types. These foundations are now ready to be composed into a coherent public API. N0011 (§8), N0014 (§11), and N0015 (§12-§13) from RFC-ROOT specify exactly what the API surface should look like.

### Constraints
1. **No runtime behavior**: This ticket defines the public API surface, types, and validation rules only. Runtime dispatch (connecting API calls to PJSUA) is deferred to P3-2 (Runtime inner + FFI).
2. **Feature gates**: `tls` and `srtp` features must be respected — TLS transport variant conditionally compiled, SRTP in AccountMediaConfig conditionally compiled.
3. **Backward compatibility**: Once published, struct field additions require `#[non_exhaustive]` or semver-major releases. All enums that may grow must be `#[non_exhaustive]`.
4. **Ownership**: All public API types must be `Send + Sync` and use `Arc<ClientInner>` for shared mutable state. Cloning SipClient must be cheap.`

**UT: [Normal] — SipClient construction & lifecycle:**

  - `sip_client_clone_is_cheap`: Cloning SipClient increments Arc refcount without deep-copying inner state.

  - `sip_client_add_account_valid`: Adding an account with valid `AccountConfig` returns `Ok(SipAccountHandle)` with correct `AccountId`.
  - `sip_client_remove_account_existing`: Removing an existing account returns `Ok(())`.
  - `sip_client_account_existing`: Querying an existing account by `AccountId` returns `Ok(SipAccountHandle)`.

**Exception 1: Actual SIP network registration and deregistration**
  - [Item/Reason] Cannot test actual SIP registration against a real server because it requires live PJSUA library and network connectivity.
  - [This is not a design defect] The feature is deterministic and testable in principle — it only requires external infrastructure unavailable in unit tests. Alternative verification via MockBackend-based integration tests validates the same logical path without network dependency.
  - [Alternative verification] MockBackend (from N0037 SipBackend trait) simulates registration responses. Existing tests/example_validation.rs validates example compilation against the public API.

**Exception 2: Actual RTP media stream setup and audio transmission**
  - [Item/Reason] Cannot test actual RTP media streaming because it requires PJSUA media engine initialization, audio device access, and real-time audio I/O.
  - [This is not a design defect] The media pipeline design is deterministic and will be tested via integration tests once the audio backend (P3-2/P4-3) is implemented. The test gap exists solely at the hardware boundary — not a design flaw.
  - [Alternative verification] OutgoingCallRequest and CallMediaPreferences struct validation are unit-tested. Audio format validation (codec policy) is tested via AccountConfig validation.

**Exception 3: TLS transport handshake and certificate validation**
  - [Item/Reason] Cannot test TLS handshake because it requires a TLS-capable transport stack, certificates, and platform-specific PKI infrastructure. The tls feature gate makes this conditionally compiled.
  - [This is not a design defect] TLS is a standard protocol with well-defined behavior. The structural guarantee (Tls variant absent without feature flag) is a type-level invariant verified at compile time — this is correct by construction, not a testing gap.
  - [Alternative verification] TlsConfig struct construction tested under #[cfg(feature = "tls")]. Compile-time assertions verify the type-level gating.

**Exception 4: ICE candidate gathering and connectivity checks (STUN/TURN)**
  - [Item/Reason] Cannot test ICE connectivity checks because they require external STUN/TURN servers and real ICE agent initialization.
  - [This is not a design defect] The ICE configuration types (IceConfig, StunServerConfig, TurnServerConfig) are data-only structs with defined validation rules — fully testable in isolation. The runtime ICE agent execution is deferred to PJSUA FFI (P3-2), which is deterministic and separately testable.

**[Happy path] — All public types compile and are accessible at crate root:**
  1. `SipClient`, `SipAccountHandle`, `ClientConfig`, `AccountConfig`, `TransportConfig` are re-exported at `siprs::*` level.
  2. `SipClient::new(ClientConfig{..})` compiles and returns `Result<SipClient, SipError>`.
  3. `SipClient::add_account(AccountConfig{..})` adds an account and returns `SipAccountHandle`.
  4. `SipAccountHandle::make_call(OutgoingCallRequest{..})` returns `Ok(CallId)`.
  5. `AccountConfig` with valid fields (non-empty username/domain/password, at least one codec) passes all validation rules.
  6. `TransportConfig::Udp(..)` / `Tcp(..)` / `Tls(..)` (with tls feature) all constructable.

**[Error case] — Invalid configurations are rejected:**
  1. `AccountConfig` with empty `username` → `Err(SipError::invalid_config(...))`.
  2. `AccountConfig` with empty `domain` → `Err(SipError::invalid_config(...))`.
  3. `AccountConfig` with empty `password` → `Err(SipError::invalid_config(...))`.
  4. `AccountCodecPolicy{enable_pcmu: false, enable_opus: false}` → validation error.
  5. `DtmfPolicy{send_methods: [], ..}` → validation error (must have at least one send method).
  6. `DtmfPolicy{receive_methods: [], ..}` → validation error (must have at least one receive method).
  7. `OutgoingCallRequest{target_uri: ""}` → validation error.
  8. `CallMediaPreferences{preferred_codecs: vec![Codec::G722]}` → validation error (only PCMU, Opus allowed).
  9. Without `tls` feature, `TransportConfig::Tls(..)` does not compile.

**[Edge case] — Boundary conditions handled correctly:**
  1. `register_on_start=false` + `allow_outbound_without_register=true` → valid config.
  2. `register_on_start=false` + `allow_outbound_without_register=false` → valid config (no-call, no-register account).
  3. `registrar_uri=None` → auto-derived as `sip:{domain}` string.
  4. `OpusConfig{complexity: 11}` → rejected (out of 0-10 range).
  5. Multiple outbound proxies, multiple custom headers → accepted.
  6. IPv6 bind addresses in transport config → accepted.
  7. ICE disabled (no STUN/TURN servers required), ICE enabled (STUN/TURN required) — structural validation.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Define `ServerConfig`, `AuthConfig`, and `AuthMode` types that specify the standalone server mode startup parameters for siprs-server — including bind address, database path, CORS origins, and authentication mode.

### Purpose
These types form the configuration contract between the siprs-server binary entry point (main.rs) and the Axum HTTP/WS server runtime. They enable declarative server configuration via CLI args (future clap integration), config files (future JSON/YAML loading), or direct struct construction for embedded Tauri usage.

### Motivation
N0061 (RFC §53) specifies the standalone server mode main.rs flow: SipClient init -> DB init -> account restore -> Axum start. Each step requires configuration parameters (bind_addr for the listener, db_path for persistence, auth for security). Without ServerConfig, these parameters would be scattered across function signatures, making the entry point untestable and configuration management ad-hoc.

### Constraints
- Must not add new crate dependencies — SocketAddr (std::net) and PathBuf (std::path) are stdlib only
- SecretString for sensitive fields requires the existing zeroize feature gate (optional dep)
- Default bind_addr must be 127.0.0.1:3910 (localhost-only for security)
- Default auth mode must be LocalhostOnly (defense-in-depth: no network-exposed API without explicit opt-in)
- serde Serialize/Deserialize must be conditionally available behind the serde feature flag (existing pattern)
- This ticket produces only data types; runtime behavior (loading config files, parsing CLI args, binding listeners) belongs to siprs-server crate (future ticket)

tickets.background:
N0012 defines AccountId/CallId/AudioSourceId as NonZeroU64 newtypes with BiMap for RuntimeId↔NativeId mapping. N0018 defines complete SipEventPayload enum with all 28+ variants across 8 categories and SipEvent wrapper with EventMeta.

### Goal
Implement the foundational ID design (NonZeroU64 newtypes + BiMap) and confirm the event model (SipEventPayload, SipEvent, EventBus, AccountEventReceiver) is fully specified with complete test coverage.

### Purpose
The ID design provides type-safe identifiers that prevent argument mix-ups (e.g., passing CallId where AccountId is expected) and enables PJSUA native ID reuse tracking via BiMap. The event model provides the crate's sole notification mechanism for all SIP lifecycle events, enabling downstream consumers to build UI updates, logging, and observability.

### Motivation
P4-1 is the structural foundation for all downstream work: every P4-* ticket (SipClient lifecycle, account/call operations, media pipeline) depends on AccountId/CallId types and the event model. Without this ticket, subsequent implementation cannot express type-safe operations or deliver events to consumers.

### Constraints
- IDs must be NonZeroU64 to match PJSUA's native id_t type (c_uint/c_ulong) while maintaining NonZero optimization (Option<AccountId> = 8 bytes)
- BiMap must handle native ID reuse without exposing stale references — the insert/remove lifecycle must be atomic per entry
- EventBus uses tokio::sync::broadcast — delivery is intentionally lossy. No ack/retry mechanism (per §15.7 N0020)
- EventModel types must remain #[non_exhaustive] for future variant addition without breaking changes

【Error case】 Attempting to construct AccountId::from_u64(0) returns None (compile-safe). BiMap::lookup on non-existent key returns None (no panic). Removing an entry from BiMap frees the NativeId for reuse. EventBus::publish to a full buffer drops oldest event (Lagged) without panicking.

【Edge case】 BiMap capacity: insert up to u64::MAX entries (theoretical limit). EventBus with capacity 1: single-slot buffer correctly delivers the most recent event after overflow. AccountEventReceiver with no matching events: blocks until matching event or sender drop (no busy loop). AccountId/CallId Ord ordering is consistent with inner NonZeroU64 ordering.

- AccountId and CallId are `u32` type aliases used across 5+ modules — migration to NonZeroU64 newtypes will touch all of them including test code
- EventModel types (SipEventPayload, SipEvent, EventMeta) are already functional; the AccountId/CallId type change is the main integration concern for P4-1

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
## Boy Scout Rule — Translatability Improvement Plan

### Code to improve

1. **id_design_newtype.rs** (new file, N0012):
   - Define `AccountId(NonZeroU64)`, `CallId(NonZeroU64)`, `AudioSourceId(NonZeroU64)` as translatable newtypes
   - Function names as verb phrases: `from_u64()` convert, `get()` retrieve, `into_native()` map
   - Variable names as domain concepts: `runtime_id`, `native_id`, `next_id` not `x`, `y`, `tmp`
   - No hardcoded values: BiMap default capacity as named constant `DEFAULT_BIMAP_CAPACITY`
   - No error swallowing: BiMap lookup returns `Option`, never `unwrap()`

2. **command_serialization.rs** (N0010, existing):
   - Replace `pub(crate) type AccountId = u32` with `use crate::model::id_design_newtype::AccountId`
   - Replace `pub(crate) type CallId = u32` with `use crate::model::id_design_newtype::CallId`
   - Same for all RuntimeCommand variant usages of these types — ensures the entire command serialization layer speaks domain nouns

3. **event_model_payload_bus.rs** (N0018, existing):
   - Update `AccountId`/`CallId` import from `concurrency_contexts::command_serialization` to `model::id_design_newtype`
   - SipEventPayload::DtmfSent variant has `#[allow(private_interfaces)]` — this resolves when AccountId is a real pub type

4. **eventbus_receiver.rs** (N0019, existing):
   - Update `AccountId` import from `command_serialization` to `model::id_design_newtype`
   - Test helpers change from `Some(1u32)` to `Some(AccountId::from_u64(1).unwrap())` — more verbose but type-safe

5. **public_api_design.rs** (N0011, existing):
   - All `AccountId`/`CallId` type references change from u32 alias to real newtype
   - `subscribe_account(account_id: 42)` becomes `subscribe_account(account_id: AccountId::try_from(42u64).unwrap())`

### Why these improve translatability
- Newtype names `AccountId`, `CallId`, `AudioSourceId` are domain nouns — the code reads as "register AccountId", "make_call returns CallId"
- `NonZeroU64` encodes the non-zero invariant in the type system, eliminating runtime checks and comments like "must be > 0"
- `BiMap::insert(runtime_id, native_id)` vs `map.put(x, y)` — named parameters tell the story
- The complete migration from `u32` to domain-specific newtypes makes every function signature self-documenting

tickets.title: Registration, Call & Shutdown State Machines

contracts.precondition: SipAccountHandle::register(), unregister(), set_registration_enabled(), registration_state() exist in the public API (public_api_design.rs) and require an internal state machine to drive registration lifecycle
contracts.postcondition: src/state/registr_state_machine.rs defines RegistrationState enum with exactly 7 variants (Disabled/Idle/Registering/Registered/Unregistering/Failed/Expired) and a try_transition() method that enforces the RFC §17 transition rules. RegistrationState is exported from state/mod.rs as pub(crate).
contracts.invariant: make_call() never checks RegistrationState — the RFC explicitly states registration and call ability are independent. Unit test asserts that the transition module does not internally gate make_call() on RegistrationState.

contracts.precondition: SipAccountHandle::make_call(), answer(), hold(), unhold(), hangup() exist in the public API and require an internal state machine to drive call lifecycle events
contracts.postcondition: src/state/call_state_model.rs defines CallState enum with exactly 13 variants (New/Calling/Trying/Ringing/EarlyMedia/Incoming/Connecting/Active/Held/Transferring/Disconnecting/Disconnected/Failed) and a try_transition() method enforcing RFC §18 outgoing/incoming/active-session transition rules. CallState is exported from state/mod.rs as pub(crate).
contracts.invariant: A new call is only created when active_call_count < ClientConfig::max_calls (u32 field in client_config_spec.rs). The invariant is enforced in the make_call() path through a guard that checks active_call_count against max_calls. Unit test covers both below-limit (allowed) and at-limit (rejected) cases.

contracts.precondition: CallState enum is defined with an Incoming variant (established by C027 postcondition)
contracts.postcondition: answer() is only semantically valid when the current CallState is Incoming. The call_state_model provides answer_permitted() or similar query that returns true only for Incoming state.
contracts.invariant: answer() returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidState) if called when current CallState is not Incoming. Unit tests verify against each non-Incoming state (New, Calling, Trying, Ringing, EarlyMedia, Connecting, Active, Held, Transferring, Disconnecting, Disconnected, Failed).

contracts.precondition: CallState is defined, providing the concept of 'active call' that audio can subscribe to
contracts.postcondition: Audio subscribe API (defined in audio_subscribe_bp.rs) distinguishes between Realtime mode (lossy, low-latency) and Lossless mode (reliable, higher-latency). The CallState model exports whether a call is in a media-active state (Ringing, EarlyMedia, Connecting, Active, Held) vs non-media state.
contracts.invariant: Realtime audio subscription is permitted for any media-active call; Lossless subscription additionally requires that the call has transitioned past Connecting into Active (media negotiated). Unit tests verify mode-per-state mapping.

contracts.precondition: SipClient has a shutdown() method (defined in public_api_design.rs) that must safely release all PJSUA resources (calls, accounts, transports)
contracts.postcondition: src/state/shutdown_specification.rs defines an idempotent shutdown sequence: (1) stop accepting new commands, (2) BYE/CANCEL all active calls, (3) unregister all accounts, (4) drain audio pipeline, (5) call pjsua_destroy. Cancellation safety: caller task cancellation must not interrupt reactor-side teardown.
contracts.invariant: shutdown() is idempotent — an AtomicBool or equivalent flag prevents re-entry. The second and subsequent calls return Ok(()) immediately without executing teardown. Unit tests verify flag prevents double-execution and concurrent calls all return Ok.

contracts.precondition: shutdown_specification.rs defines the shutdown state (postcondition of C044)
contracts.postcondition: M20 RuntimeCommand routing during shutdown is specified: GetAccountInfo is permitted (read-only state query), ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect are rejected with InvalidState('shutting down'). All other commands are also rejected.
contracts.invariant: GetAccountInfo returns a response (not Err) during shutdown with a shutting_down: bool flag. ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect return Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidState) with message containing 'shutting down'. Unit tests verify each command's behaviour against the shutdown state.

tickets.background:
N0025 defines RegistrationState enum (7 states: Disabled/Idle/Registering/Registered/Unregistering/Failed/Expired) with transition rules. N0026 defines CallState enum (12 states: New/Calling/Trying/Ringing/EarlyMedia/Incoming/Connecting/Active/Held/Transferring/Disconnecting/Disconnected/Failed) with outgoing/incoming diagrams. N0043 defines idempotent shutdown sequence.

### Goal
Define and implement the three state machines that govern the lifecycle of registration, calls, and shutdown in the siprs crate. Each state machine must be fully typed (Rust enum), enforce RFC-defined transition rules, and expose a try_transition() interface for the runtime module.

### Purpose
These state machines are the backbone of siprs correctness. Without them, the runtime cannot enforce legal call flows (e.g., answer only on incoming), manage concurrency limits (max_calls), or guarantee safe teardown without resource leaks. They exist to make illegal states unrepresentable and to provide a single source of truth for state-dependent operations.

### Motivation
Currently all three state machine files are stubs (pub enum State {} with a STUB marker). The runtime module (P3-2) and the public API (P3-1) depend on these types being defined before they can dispatch commands. Without this ticket, the entire runtime layer is blocked. The state machine definitions themselves are purely structural enums with transition validation — no FFI or I/O — making them the ideal first concrete implementation in the crate.

### Constraints
- RegistrationState must remain independent from call ability (no cross-gating per §17)
- CallState must contain exactly 13 variants as specified by §18; no more, no fewer
- Shutdown MUST be idempotent (AtomicBool guard) to prevent double-free of PJSUA resources
- No external dependencies beyond std and crate-internal types (SipError, SipErrorKind)
- All three state modules must be pub(crate) and exported from state/mod.rs
- The existing RegistrationState enum in public_api_design.rs (4-variant) is the public API type; the internal 7-variant RegistrationState in registr_state_machine.rs is a separate, more granular state machine for runtime use

testExceptions: Cancellation safety of shutdown() — impossible to test via unit tests because the shutdown sequence (BYE/CANCEL, unregister, drain audio, pjsua_destroy) involves FFI calls into PJSUA. Unit tests cannot instantiate a real pjsua instance without native libraries and platform-specific setup. The shutdown state machine core (idempotent flag, transition validation) is fully unit-testable. This is not an architectural defect — the FFI boundary is part of the design and integration tests cover the cancellation scenario by spawning a tokio task for shutdown(), cancelling the caller, and observing EventBus events for completion.

PJSUA native state correlation — impossible to test via unit tests because the pjsua native API can only be queried through FFI at runtime. There is no compile-time mechanism to assert RegistrationState and CallState equivalence with pjsua_acc_info and pjsua_call_info. The BiMap correlation pattern (P4-1) is verified by separate unit tests. This is not an architectural defect — the FFI boundary is inherently integration-test-only in this project's design and the state machine transition logic is independently verified by unit tests.
acceptanceCriteria: [Happy path] Registration, call, and shutdown lifecycle: Create SipClient, add account, register (Disabled→Registering→Registered), make_call (New→Calling→Trying→Ringing→Connecting→Active), hold/unhold (Active→Held→Active), hangup (Active→Disconnecting→Disconnected), unregister (Registered→Unregistering→Idle), shutdown (Idle→ShuttingDown→ShutdownComplete). All transitions validate successfully, no errors returned.

[Error case] Invalid transitions and flow control: Attempt unregister from Idle (should fail InvalidState), attempt answer() on Outgoing/Ringing call state (should fail InvalidState), attempt make_call when active_calls >= max_calls (should fail InvalidState), attempt shutdown twice (second call returns Ok but no-op), attempt ConfConnect during shutdown (should fail InvalidState with 'shutting down'). All assertions confirmed.

[Edge case] Boundary and absorbing states: RegistrationState::Disabled — only register() valid, all other transitions rejected. CallState::Failed — no valid transitions from terminal state. CallState::Disconnected — no valid transitions, absorbing. Shutdown with 0 active calls and 0 accounts — teardown completes Ok with no actual work but no errors. max_calls=0 — all make_call() attempts rejected without creating call state. RegistrationState::Expired→Registering — re-registration from expiry succeeds.
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps]
  1. Define RegistrationState enum + try_transition() in registr_state_machine.rs
  2. Define CallState enum + try_transition() in call_state_model.rs
  3. Define ShutdownState enum + idempotent guard + M20 routing in shutdown_specification.rs
  4. Export all three from state/mod.rs
  5. Write failing tests (Red phase — this spec's testUnit)
  6. Implement to pass (Green phase)
  7. Refactor (Boy Scout rule)

- [Risks]
  - Risk: The try_transition() function signatures need to align with the future runtime module's expected interface. Mitigation: make try_transition(&self, target) -> Result<(), SipError> simple and generic; the runtime can wrap it as needed.
  - Risk: The 7-variant RegistrationState differs from the 4-variant public RegistrationState in public_api_design.rs. Mitigation: the runtime maps between them; the spec documents this explicitly.

- [Caveats]
  - The internal RegistrationState (7 variants) and public RegistrationState (4 variants: Unregistered/Registering/Registered/Failed) coexist. They are NOT the same type. The public one's Unregistered maps to the internal Disabled or Idle depending on context.
  - The Transferring state in CallState is transient — the runtime must never leave a call in Transferring indefinitely. A timeout or NOTIFY resolves it.

- [Open items]
  - Whether try_transition should consume self or take &self depends on the runtime's ownership model. Currently designed as &self (borrowing) to avoid unnecessary cloning in the runtime's state map lookup.
  - The exact mapping between internal RegistrationState (7) and public RegistrationState (4) needs to be confirmed during runtime implementation (P3-2).

- [Future improvements]
  - Add proptest-based property testing to verify the transition matrix against a formal specification (all reachable states, no dead ends beyond defined terminals).
  - Integrate state machine visualisation (Mermaid diagram auto-generated from enum transitions) for documentation.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal establishment] Preconditions that must hold for correct behavior:
  - RegistrationState transitions must follow the RFC §17 transition matrix (Disabled→Registering→Registered→Unregistering→Idle cycle, with Failed/Expired paths)
  - CallState transitions must follow the RFC §18 transition matrix (outgoing: New→Calling→Trying→[Ringing|EarlyMedia]→Connecting→Active; incoming: New→Incoming→Connecting→Active; active-session: Active↔Held, Active→Transferring→[Active|Disconnecting])
  - Shutdown sequence must execute in order: BYE/CANCEL all calls → unregister accounts → drain audio → pjsua_destroy

- [Error invariant] Invariants that must never be violated even on error:
  - A failed transition must never leave the state machine in an inconsistent/undefined state — if try_transition() returns Err, the current state is unchanged (atomicity)
  - Even if PJSUA native calls fail during shutdown, the internal ShutdownState must still advance; the idempotent guard prevents re-entry regardless of PJSUA errors
  - max_calls violation must reject the call without creating any CallState entry; no orphan state on rejection

- [Internal state invariant] Invariants the module's internal state must always satisfy:
  - RegistrationState enum value is always one of exactly 7 valid variants (no undefined state)
  - CallState enum value is always one of exactly 13 valid variants
  - ShutdownState transitions only forward: Idle → ShuttingDown → ShutdownComplete; never backward
  - The AtomicBool shutdown guard and the ShutdownState enum must be consistent (guard=true iff state != Idle)

- [Boundary invariant] Invariants related to boundary values / thresholds:
  - max_calls = 0 means no outgoing calls permitted (all make_call() attempts rejected). This is a valid config allowed by ClientConfig validation.
  - max_calls = u32::MAX means effectively unlimited calls (constrained only by system resources)
  - Disabled state in RegistrationState: once set, all non-register transitions are invalid until register() or set_enabled(true) is called
  - Failed and Disconnected/DisconnectedStates are absorbing — once entered, no further transitions are valid
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] State transitions are logged via tracing::info! or tracing::debug! at the transition boundary. Each RegistrationState::try_transition() and CallState::try_transition() call emits a structured log: transition(from=%?state, to=%?target, result=%?result). ShutdownState transitions emit tracing::info! with the step description and result. Log level: info for state transitions, debug for internal validation.

- [Metrics] Track state machine counters via atomic integers: REGISTRATION_STATE_COUNT[7] tracking current state distribution, CALL_STATE_COUNT[13] tracking current call state distribution, SHUTDOWN_COUNT tracking shutdown invocations. These are exposed via the observability module (src/config/observability_metrics.rs). All counters are pub(crate) AtomicU64 statics initialized to zero.

- [Error tracking] Invalid transition attempts are logged at warn level with the invalid (from, to) pair. This is a design invariant violation that should never trigger in normal operation — its occurrence indicates a bug in the calling code (runtime layer). A malformed transition is not an external error path; it is an internal invariant failure.

- [Health check] The health check endpoint (future, P5-x) monitors: (a) total active calls vs max_calls ratio, (b) the number of RegistrationState::Failed accounts, (c) whether ShutdownState has been entered (for post-mortem diagnostics). These provide early warning of resource exhaustion and failed registrations.

tickets.background:
- 【Goal】Implement the foundational audio data model (SampleRate, BitDepth, ChannelLayout, AudioFormat, AudioChunkPair), the IN/OUT Pair Alignment algorithm (PairAligner with timestamped ring buffers), the resample pipeline (ResamplePipeline using rubato with stereo L=IN/R=OUT), the codec policy & fallback rules (NegotiatedCodec, CodecSelectionPolicy, PCMU=254/Opus=255 only), and the media bridge architecture (RustMediaPort with lock-free queue boundary and capture/playback tap ports). These five subcomponents form the complete audio pipeline for siprs.
- 【Purpose】The audio pipeline is the core processing path between PJSIP's real-time media thread and zasso's async AudioWorkerTask. AudioFormat provides the type-safe representation of sample rates, bit depths, and channel layouts. AudioChunkPair unifies bidirectional audio into a single timestamped container for alignment. PairAligner resolves RTP-vs-mixer timing skew with tolerance-based matching. ResamplePipeline converts between codec rates via rubato. CodecPolicy enforces that only PCMU and Opus are used, with a defined fallback order. MediaBridge (RustMediaPort) provides the lock-free queue boundary that separates RT callback from async context.
- 【Motivation】These five subcomponents are the foundational audio primitives required before any higher-level audio feature (mixer, source lifecycle, echo cancellation, volume control) can be implemented. They are mandated by the RFC graph (N0030, N0035, N0036, N0040, N0049) and are prerequisites for P5-2 (AudioMixer & AudioWorkerTask implementation). Without these types, the audio pipeline cannot be expressed at the type level — execution order is N0030→N0035→N0036→N0040→N0049→N0033→N0034 (P5-2).
- 【Constraints】(1) Audio-only: no video, recording, or GUI types in this module. (2) FFI-dependent subcomponents (rubato, crossbeam) are designed as injectable/structural types — actual FFI calls deferred to P0-9. (3) PairAligner operates in AudioWorkerTask (Tokio async context), NOT in RT callback — VecDeque operations are safe. (4) RustMediaPort is an architectural design only (types and concepts) — actual FFI callbacks unsafe code is P0-9 responsibility. (5) NegotiatedCodec and CodecSelectionPolicy must integrate with existing AccountConfig (P3-1) and m20_codec_auto_mode (N0041). (6) No new external crate dependencies without RFC approval — rubato and crossbeam are gated behind P5-2 when actual implementation begins.

tickets.background:
N0062 specifies REST API endpoint table (18 endpoints), WebSocket endpoints, Axum router structure, WS message protocol (JSON text + binary audio frames with fixed 24-byte header), and event-audio correlation via sequence numbers. N0064 specifies SQLite + SeaORM persistence with table schemas (accounts, transport_configs, client_settings, tls_configs) and migration management.

### Goal
Implement the complete HTTP/WebSocket API protocol surface (REST endpoint path constants, WS binary frame header, WS text event protocol, Axum Router builder, AppState, handler function signatures) and SQLite persistence layer (4 table schemas as SQL const strings, SeaORM migration management trait, migration path constant) for the siprs standalone server mode.

### Purpose
The HTTP/WS API is the external interface through which zasso UI clients and external tools interact with the siprs SIP engine — without it, the standalone server cannot receive commands or stream events. SQLite persistence ensures account configurations, transport settings, client preferences, and TLS certificate configurations survive server restarts, eliminating the need to reconfigure on every startup.

### Motivation
These are the two remaining architectural foundations required before the siprs-server binary can be assembled. Every previous P4 ticket has established the SIP engine internals (IDs, events, state machines, audio pipeline) — P4-4 provides the external network-facing interface and the configuration persistence layer. Without this ticket, the standalone server would have no API to receive commands and no way to persist configuration.

### Constraints
(1) Audio-only: REST and WS protocols are for SIP control and audio streaming only — no video, screen-sharing, or recording endpoints. (2) Sequence number sharing: The global u64 sequence number space is shared between SipEvent and AudioChunkPair — must be monotonically increasing and consistent across both types. (3) AudioFrameHeader is #[repr(C, packed)] for FFI compatibility with PJSIP media thread — must be exactly 24 bytes. (4) No new external crate dependencies added in this ticket — endpoint paths and type definitions use std library and existing crate types only. (5) JWT auth middleware is defined in a separate file (src/security/auth_jwt_middleware.rs, P2-4) — this ticket defines the interfaces (public route list, auth request/response types) that the middleware consumes. (6) SQL schema constants are pure string definitions in this ticket — actual rusqlite/SeaORM runtime integration happens in siprs-server binary ticket.

tickets.background:
# Background

## Goal
P5-1 implements SIP call control API (answer/hangup/hold/unhold/transfer/send_dtmf/call_state), RawSipMessage Authorization redaction, and AudioSubscribe API (AudioTapHandle + AudioTapMode) on SipClient, concretizing the design contracts of RFC-ROOT sections 16(N0024)/19(N0027)/22(N0031) as code.

## Purpose
Enable SipClient consumers (zasso upper layers) to control the full SIP call lifecycle (answer/disconnect/hold/transfer/DTMF/state). Also provide access to call audio (subscribe_audio) and safe raw SIP message retrieval (Authorization redaction) as the foundation for monitoring, recording, and quality measurement.

## Motivation
P4-4 (HTTP/WS Protocol types & SQLite schema) and P4-3 (Audio Format/PairAligner/Resampler) have established foundational types. P5-1 is the first phase implementing actual call control APIs using these types, positioned as a type-definition and contract-verification layer that does not depend on P6 (Runtime + Backend).

## Constraints
- No PJSIP FFI dependency (deferred to P6): implement via RuntimeCommand indirect dispatch, test with mock PjsuaBackend
- No new dependency crates: use only tokio (mpsc, oneshot) and std::collections standard features
- AudioTapHandle does not need Sync + Send (used within a single task)
- All SipClient methods are async fn with Result<T, SipError> return type
- Maintain existing pub(crate) visibility for RawSipMessage
scope: RawSipMessage: direction, transport, headers, body, redact_authorization
Call control: answer (180/183/200/486/603), hangup, hold, unhold, transfer, send_dtmf, call_state
AudioTapMode: Realtime (oldest-drop) and Lossless (backpressure)
AudioTapHandle with recv()
SubscribeAudio Reactor handler with conf_connect and MediaDirection

Before: stub trait only. After: impl SipClient { pub async fn answer(&self, call_id: CallId, code: u16) -> Result<(), SipError>; ... }. API contract: adds 7 new public async methods to SipClient. Schema: unchanged. Config: unchanged. Dep: none.
  - src/api/audio_subscribe_bp.rs — modify: replace empty `pub trait Service {}` stub with AudioTapMode enum, AudioTapHandle struct, MediaDirection enum, and subscribe_audio SipClient method. Before: stub trait only. After: AudioTapMode (Realtime/Lossless), AudioTapHandle { rx }, MediaDirection (Inbound/Outbound/Both), SipClient::subscribe_audio(). API contract: adds AudioTapMode, AudioTapHandle, MediaDirection types and subscribe_audio method. Schema: unchanged. Config: unchanged. Dep: tokio::sync::mpsc (already present).

Non-changes (out of scope):

  - CallState machine implementation — already handled by P4-2. Why: call_state() reads the existing state; does not modify it.

testUnit: UT: [Normal] Valid parameters for all call control APIs — `answer(CallId::from_u64(1).unwrap(), 200)` returns Ok(()); `hangup(CallId::from_u64(1).unwrap(), HangupReason::Normal)` returns Ok(()); `hold(CallId::from_u64(1).unwrap())` returns Ok(()); `unhold(CallId::from_u64(1).unwrap())` returns Ok(()); `send_dtmf(CallId::from_u64(1).unwrap(), "123", DtmfMethod::Rfc2833)` returns Ok(()); `call_state(CallId::from_u64(1).unwrap())` returns Ok(CallState); `transfer(CallId::from_u64(1).unwrap(), "sip:target@domain")` returns Ok(()). All calls dispatched via RuntimeCommand channel and resolved through RuntimeCommand sequential processing. `answer(code)` accepts 180, 183, 200, 486, 603 as valid response codes; `SipClient` methods delegate to `RuntimeCommand` (call_api_semantics.rs → concurrency_contexts dispatcher). [C028-precondition: CallState states (New, Calling, Trying, Ringing, EarlyMedia, Incoming, Connecting, Active, Held, Transferring, Disconnecting, Disconnected, Failed) are defined and accessible via CallState::try_transition(). The call API is built on top of these states — answer() guard uses CallState::is_answer_permitted() which validates state == Incoming.]

UT: [Normal] RawSipMessage `redact_authorization` removes Authorization and Proxy-Authorization header values — given a RawSipMessage with headers containing "Authorization: Digest token=abc123", calling `msg.redact_authorization()` returns a new RawSipMessage where the value is replaced with "***REDACTED***". Proxy-Authorization similarly redacted. Non-sensitive headers (Content-Type, Contact, etc.) are untouched. Construct AudioTapHandle::new(mpsc::channel(16)) and verify recv() returns Some(AudioChunkPair) when data is sent; returns None when channel is closed. AudioTapMode::Realtime creates oldest-drop channel; AudioTapMode::Lossless creates bounded backpressure channel.

UT: [Error] `answer()` on non-Incoming call returns SipError with kind InvalidState — given a call in state Active, Calling, or Held, answer(200) returns Err containing "answer() is only valid for incoming calls". `hangup()` on already-Disconnected call returns SipError(CallNotFound). `hold()` on already-Held call returns SipError(InvalidState) with message "call is already on hold". `unhold()` on non-Held call returns SipError(InvalidState). `transfer()` with empty target string returns SipError(InvalidConfig). `send_dtmf()` with empty digits returns SipError(InvalidConfig). `subscribe_audio()` on non-existent call_id returns SipError(CallNotFound). RawSipMessage redact_authorization on empty headers yields empty result with no panic.

UT: [Boundary] `answer()` with all 5 valid codes (180, 183, 200, 486, 603) on Incoming call — each returns Ok(()). Code 0 or 700+ returns SipError(InvalidConfig). Multiple rapid call_state() queries from concurrent tasks all resolve to the same consistent state (proved via tokio::spawn barrier). AudioTapHandle::recv() with capacity=0 on Lossless mode: construction itself succeeds but first send blocks (backpressure). AudioTapMode::Realtime with capacity=1: oldest-drop replaces message when not consumed in time, returning overflow error via SipError(AudioPipelineBroken). `send_dtmf()` digits exceeding 32 chars returns SipError(InvalidConfig) per RFC 4733 limit.

UT: [Invariant] Call state transitions remain consistent — after answer() returns Ok, subsequent call_state() returns state != Incoming (transitions to Connecting or Active depending on answer code). After hangup(), call_state() returns Disconnected state. After hold(), call_state() returns Held. After unhold() on Held call, call_state() returns Active. Multiple answer() calls on same call return Err(InvalidState) after first success — invariant: single answer per call. AudioTapHandle lifecycle: once AudioTapHandle is dropped, subsequent recv() on any clone returns None (channel closed). RawSipMessage fields: start_line, headers, body, text, content_length, remote_addr, local_addr remain consistent after redact_authorization (only header values change, not structure). [C029-invariant: DtmfMethod in call API supports three methods — Inband (sent as RFC 2833 events in audio stream), Info (sent as SIP INFO messages), Rfc2833 (explicit RFC 4733 stream events). DtmfMethod is an enum imported from config::account_config_spec with variants Inband, Info, Rfc2833, InfoSipInfo — at least the first three satisfy the contract invariant. C033-invariant: AudioTapHandle exposes an ErasedAudioSource interface via its recv() method — the fact that recv() returns Option<AudioChunkPair> (not a concrete source trait) satisfies the erased abstraction. The AudioTapHandle type itself is the erased audio source for P5-1; the AsyncAudioSource trait (RPITIT) implementation is deferred to N0032/P5-2 where the concrete source adapter is built.]
testIntegration: IT: [Integration point] `SipClient::answer()` dispatches through RuntimeCommand channel → Reactor::process_command_queue() → PjsuaBackend::call_answer(). The RuntimeCommand::AnswerCall payload carries (CallId, u16 code, oneshot::Sender<Result<(), SipError>>). Verification calls the SipClient method and waits on the oneshot receiver for the result. Similar pattern for hold/unhold/transfer/dtmf/call_state/subscribe_audio — all flow through RuntimeCommand → Reactor → PjsuaBackend triple.

IT: [Verification] Each integration test constructs a SipClient (via SipClient::new()), adds an account, and makes/receives a simulated call through a mock PjsuaBackend. The mock backend verifies that the correct native PJSUA API would be invoked with the right parameters. For AudioTapMode, the integration test verifies that ConfConnect RuntimeCommand is emitted when subscribe_audio is called, and that AudioTapHandle receives AudioChunkPair frames from the mock media pipeline.

IT: [Prerequisites] P3-2 (RuntimeHandle + CommandSender/Receiver wiring) must be implemented for command dispatch. P3-1 (SipClient scaffolding with Arc<ClientInner>) must be in place — currently exists as stub. P4-2 (Call state machine transition table) must be complete for call_state() to return correct state. PjsuaBackend mock (P6-2) must be available for simulation. AudioFormat/AudioChunkPair types (P4-3) must exist — currently implemented. CallId, AccountId newtypes (P4-1) — implemented.

IT: [Related tickets] P3-2 (RuntimeHandle + RuntimeCommand dispatch), P3-1 (SipClient scaffolding), P4-2 (Call state machine), P4-1 (ID newtypes), P6-2 (PjsuaBackend mock), P4-3 (AudioFormat, AudioChunkPair), P0-4 (EventBus), P0-5 (SipError design — completed). P0-7 (DtmfSentInfo/DtmfMethod/DtmfConfig two-phase — defines DtmfMethod).
testExceptions: Exception entry: Real PJSUA FFI call_answer/hangup/hold FFI calls. impossible to test: Real PJSIP calls require a running PJSIP library instance with real SIP transport which this crate cannot mock at the FFI level — the pjsua_call_answer() FFI function signature (extern "C") is fixed and its behavior depends on a live pjsua state. This is not a design defect: the system is explicitly layered with Command/Reactor/Backend pattern, where RuntimeCommand dispatch (verified in P5-1) abstracts the FFI boundary, and PjsuaBackend (P6-2) implements the real FFI calls. Alternative verification: Integration tests marked #[ignore] for CI-only runs using Docker Asterisk (P6-2) exercise the full Command→Reactor→Backend chain.

Exception entry: AudioTapHandle real-time audio streaming under OS scheduling. impossible to test: Deterministic behavior under OS scheduling (context switches, interrupt latency, thread preemption) cannot be unit-tested because the OS scheduler is not under test control. This is not a design defect: the AudioTapHandle abstraction cleanly separates channel semantics (tokio::mpsc::channel send/recv — synchronously testable) from OS scheduling (system-level). This separation proves it is not a design defect. Alternative verification: E2E tests with Docker Asterisk (P6-3) using real audio generation/consumption exercise the full scheduling path.

Exception entry: RawSipMessage Authorization redaction with malformed headers (e.g., "Authorization" vs "authorization" casing). impossible to test: SIP headers are case-insensitive per RFC 3261, and header parsing/normalization is the responsibility of the upstream PJSIP callback layer (P0-4 EventBus raw SIP channel), not the redaction logic which operates on pre-normalized key-value pairs. This is not a design defect: the separation of concerns is intentional — the redaction function is a pure transformation on the normalized data structure. Alternative verification: Header casing normalization is verified in P0-4 integration tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Happy path: SipClient::answer(CallId, 200) on an incoming call returns Ok(()). The call state transitions from Incoming → Connecting → Active via the state machine. SipClient::hangup() on the Active call returns Ok(()), and call_state() returns Disconnected. SipClient::hold() returns Ok(()) and call_state() returns Held. SipClient::unhold() returns Ok(()) and call_state() returns Active. SipClient::transfer(call_id, "sip:target@domain") returns Ok(()). SipClient::send_dtmf(call_id, "123", DtmfMethod::Rfc2833) returns Ok(()). All operations complete without panic and produce the correct CallState transitions.

Error case: SipClient::answer() on a non-existent call_id returns Err(SipError { kind: CallNotFound }). SipClient::hangup() on an already-Disconnected call returns Err(SipError { kind: CallNotFound }). SipClient::hold() on a call in New state returns Err(SipError { kind: InvalidState, message: "hold() is only valid for Active calls" }). SipClient::subscribe_audio() on a non-existent call returns Err(SipError { kind: CallNotFound }). SipClient methods never panic; all error paths return typed SipError.

Edge case: SipClient::answer(code=180) returns Ok(()) and keeps the call in Ringing state (provisional). Answer(code=183) allows early media. Answer(code=486/603) declines the call and transitions to Disconnected. RawSipMessage with empty header vector: redact_authorization() returns clone with no changes. AudioTapHandle::recv() on a closed channel returns None (channel closure is not an error). Multiple concurrent call_state() queries for the same call_id all return the same state (proved via tokio::spawn).

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal establishment] For each call, exactly one CallState is active at any time. The state transitions follow the 13-state matrix defined in N0026/CallState::try_transition(). AudioTapHandle lifecycle: handle exists only while the underlying call is active and subscribe_audio consumer has not dropped the handle.
- [Invariant on error] Even when call_state() returns Err (e.g., call not found), no internal state corruption occurs — the CallState machine stays in its last valid state. Authorization redaction failure (e.g., malformed header key) never panics; the header is returned unmodified.
- [Internal state invariant] SipClient.call_state() returns the state from the authoritative runtime state (not a local cache). RuntimeCommand ordering is FIFO — two consecutive commands on the same call_id are processed in submission order. AudioTapHandle's internal mpsc::Receiver is consumed only by recv(); no concurrent access.
- [Boundary invariant] answer() codes are restricted to {180, 183, 200, 486, 603}. Code 0 and codes >= 700 are rejected. send_dtmf() digits max length = 32 (RFC 4733).
